story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o2.tex: See Jo'vassa to the temple steps
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o2.top: You made it. How are the knees?
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.offer: You look like you could use company on the road.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.outro: I escorted the pilgrim Jo'vassa safely to the Moon Temple, clearing the bandits who prey on the faithful along the way.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.pitch: Company, and a sword to go with it. This one is walking to the Moon Temple in the hills to give thanks for a grandson. The road is full of bandits who think pilgrims carry gold. This one carries only sugar cakes, but bandits do not ask first.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.title: The Pilgrim's Path
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.de: Skooma-cooks raided the temple's moon sugar fields outside Torval. Hadoba sent me to recover the consecrated sugar before it was boiled into skooma.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.o0: Find the skooma-cooks' camp south of Torval
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.o1: Two of them were too far gone on their own product to feel the blows. I felt sorry for them, a little, afterwards.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.o3: The moons thank you, and so does Hadoba's sweet tooth. Remember: sugar is holy. Skooma is sugar that has forgotten what it is for. So are some Khajiit.
Return the sugar to Moon-Bishop Hadoba
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.of: What would you have an Initiate do?
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.ou: I broke up a skooma camp outside Torval and returned the temple's consecrated moon sugar to Hadoba.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.pi: Moon sugar is the Lattice made solid, the light of the moons caught in a grain. Skooma-cooks have raided the temple fields and carried our sugar to a camp south of the city, to boil it into poison. Bring it home before it is ruined.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.desc: Moon-Bishop Hadoba of Torval agreed to teach me the faith of the Khajiit, beginning with the Riddle'Thar, the divine order of the moons.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o0.r: Good. Hadoba only sends those who might listen. We will wait for the moons together. They are always late, and always exactly on time.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o0.t: The Moon-Bishop sent me to walk with you.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o2.r: Jone and Jode. Masser and Secunda. They move in a pattern, the Lattice, and a Khajiit's shape depends on how they stood at birth. All of us, cathay and senche and the little alfiq, are one people dancing under two lights. That is the first riddle.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o2.t: The moons are up. What am I looking for?
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o3.c: That every shape of Khajiit is one people.
Yes. The Riddle'Thar ended our clan wars by reminding us whose children we are. Welcome, Initiate.
That the moons move in a pattern nobody can change.
Hm. Nobody should change. Some try. That is a story for later. Still: welcome, Initiate.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.offe: I'd like to learn the ways of the Moon-Priests.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.outr: I watched the moons rise with Moon-Priest Azadhi and learned the first lesson of the Riddle'Thar. Moon-Bishop Hadoba accepted me as an Initiate.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.pitc: Then you must first learn the Riddle'Thar, the order the moons gave our people when we were scattered and quarrelling. It is not difficult. It is only true. Walk with Azadhi under the moons tonight, and come back and tell Hadoba what you saw.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.desc: Hadoba has sent me to the Moon Temple, where Azadhi will teach me the Two-Moons Dance, the ritual that is also a way of life. Hadoba warns me that the darkness does not like to watch it.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o1.t: Wait for both moons to rise
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o2.r: Nobody does. That is the point.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o2.t: I'm ready, though I don't know the steps.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o3.c: Follow Jone, the bright moon of law and order.
Steady steps. Good. Jone keeps the pattern so the rest of us can stray a little.
Follow Jode, the pale moon of change.
Quick steps. Good. Jode reminds the pattern that it is alive.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o4.j: The shadow came out of the gap between the moons' light. It did not like being seen. When it fled, the singers did not even miss a note.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o4.t: Drive off the shadow that comes to break the Dance
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o5.r: Ruin it? Walker, that was the Dance. The darkness always comes to watch. The trick is to keep dancing. Hadoba will hear of this, and then, this one suspects, so will the Mane.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o5.t: It's gone. Did I ruin the Dance?
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.outr: I joined the Two-Moons Dance at the Moon Temple and drove off a shadow of Namiira that came to break it. Azadhi says the Mane will hear of it.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.de: The Mane has summoned me to Riverhold. Hadoba warns that Renrijra Krin rebels have been seen near the city, and they would like nothing better than to embarrass the Mane in front of the faithful.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.o1: The Mane knows. The Mane also knows that knives are waiting on the hill road behind the palace. The Renrijra Krin believe a dead priest makes a fine joke. Show them it does not.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.o2: The Laughing Knife laughed right up until the end. I think it was genuine. The Renrijra find a great many things funny that are not.
Ambush the Renrijra Krin on the hill road
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.o3: Good. Then come before the moons and the people.
The hill road is clear. No one is laughing.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.ou: I stopped a Renrijra Krin ambush outside Riverhold. Before the moons and the faithful, the Mane named me a Moon-Bishop and one of the Voices of the Mane.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.de: Eno Hlaalu has deciphered the Brotherhood letter. Their cell hides in an abandoned Velothi tomb west of Vivec. He has signed a writ for every one of them.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o0: An abandoned tomb west of Vivec. Here is the writ. It names the whole cell, and it is the first of its kind in a hundred years. Go.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o2: Execute the writ on the Brotherhood assassins
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o3: I left the Grandmaster's writ on the altar of their tomb. When the Brotherhood comes looking, they will know it was lawful, and who signed it.
Kill the cell's leader, the Speaker Darvame Hleran
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o4: Then stand there and hear me.
The writ is served. The cell is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.ou: I served the Grandmaster's writ on the Dark Brotherhood's cell in Vvardenfell. Eno Hlaalu named me an Exalted Master of the Morag Tong.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.desc: Ethasi Rilvayn of the Morag Tong hall in Balmora will accept me if I learn the code and execute a sanctioned writ against Ovys Hlerano, an extortionist.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o0.r: Listen closely. I will not say it twice.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o0.t: Hear the code of the Morag Tong
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o1.j: I left the writ folded on Hlerano's chest, as the code requires. The farmers he burned out will know who answered them, and that it was lawful.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o1.t: Execute the writ on Ovys Hlerano
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o2.r: And you left the writ. Good. You are an Associate of the Morag Tong. Mephala watches us all. Try to make her proud.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o2.t: The writ is served. Hlerano is dead.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.offe: I want to join the Morag Tong.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.outr: I executed a sanctioned writ against Ovys Hlerano and joined the Morag Tong.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.pitc: Then you will learn the code, and then you will carry a writ. Ovys Hlerano, an extortionist who burned a family's farm when they refused to pay him, has been sentenced. He drinks at a shack on the road south of town. Leave this writ on his body.
story.skycraft.q.mt_threads_of_the_websp: Mephala, the Webspinner, blessed the Morag Tong with sacred threads. Three have been lost: one at her shrine, one in the ruin of Yansirramus, and one in the hands of a renegade in Vivec. Eno Hlaalu wants them home.
Travel to the shrine of Mephala
Kill the spiders nesting in the shrine
Take the thread from the shrine
Travel to the ruin of Yansirramus
Banish the daedra guarding the ruin
Find the renegade Ralvas Indrano in Vivec and take back his thread
Return the first thread to Eno Hlaalu
Indrano's thread. He won't need it now.
I returned the three Threads of the Webspinner to Eno Hlaalu. Mephala herself has bid the Tong cut the Dark Brotherhood out of Morrowind.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_captain_mavus.d: Ethasi Rilvayn gave me a writ for Captain Seleth Mavus, a smuggler running skooma and slaves through the docks of Ebonheart.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_captain_mavus.o: Fight through Mavus's crew on the docks
When Mavus fell, the hold was opened. The captives inside walked out into the sun and did not look back.
Execute the writ on Captain Seleth Mavus
The writ said nothing about the cargo. The code says nothing against kindness, either. Well done.
Mavus is dead, and his cargo set free.
Do you have another writ for me?
I served the writ on Captain Seleth Mavus at Ebonheart, and his captives walked free.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_captain_mavus.p: Captain Seleth Mavus runs skooma through Ebonheart on a hull full of slaves. The Council sealed the writ yesterday. His crew will fight; the writ names only him, but the code permits you to defend yourself.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_ser_andalas.des: A writ has been sealed against Ser Varo Andalas, a Vivec noble who poisoned his cousin and bought the magistrates' silence.
Andalas offered me his cousin's inheritance to walk away. I left the writ on his desk instead, beside the bribes he had been counting.
Execute the writ on Ser Varo Andalas
Of course he did, and of course you didn't. That is the whole difference between us and the hired knives. Grandmaster Hlaalu has heard your name.
Andalas offered me gold to leave. I didn't take it.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_ser_andalas.out: I served the writ on Ser Varo Andalas in Vivec and refused his bribe.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_ser_andalas.pit: A delicate one. Ser Varo Andalas, a minor noble of Vivec, poisoned his own cousin for an inheritance and bribed the magistrates to look away. His cousin's widow came to us. The Council agreed. He keeps guards, and he keeps them close.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_the_infiltrator: Grandmaster Eno Hlaalu has issued a writ against Fevila Sarano, a Dark Brotherhood assassin hiding in Balmora who murdered members of the Morag Tong.
The quiet one who never takes coin from anyone? Odd for a clerk. She keeps a room above the old warehouse on the east bank.
Ask Nevos the factor about the clerk Fevila Sarano
There's a clerk named Fevila Sarano. Where can I find her?
Execute the writ on Fevila Sarano
A Brotherhood cipher. I can read it, given time. Meanwhile, there is a matter of faith to attend to. Mephala's threads have gone astray, and we will need her favour for what comes next.
Bring the coded letter to Eno Hlaalu
Sarano is dead. She carried this.
I executed the Dark Brotherhood infiltrator Fevila Sarano in Balmora. Her coded letter will lead us to the Brotherhood's cell in Vvardenfell.

Two of our members have been murdered in their beds, without writs. That is not our way, and it is not the way of anyone in Morrowind. The Dark Brotherhood has come to Vvardenfell. One of them hides in Balmora as a moneylender's clerk, Fevila Sarano. Here is the writ.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.desc: Chief Burguk gro-Dushnikh of Dushnikh Yal will consider me as Blood-Kin if I kill the giant that has been killing the stronghold's herds.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o0.journa: The giant had a goat under each arm when I found it, and it did not want to give either of them back.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o0.text: Kill the giant raiding Dushnikh Yal's herds
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o1.text: Take a knucklebone from the giant
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o2.reply: A good bone, from a big one. It will make a fine charm against sickness for the little ones. Go and tell Burguk the wise-woman is satisfied. He will pretend that does not matter to him.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o2.text: Bring the knucklebone to Murbul the wise-woman
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o2.topic: Chief Burguk said you'd want this.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o3.reply: Then you have fed the stronghold instead of eating from it. That is the beginning of being Orc. You are Blood-Kin to Dushnikh Yal. Eat with us tonight, and do not complain about the food.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o3.topic: The giant is dead, and Murbul has her bone.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.offer: I want to earn a place among the Orcs.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.outro: I killed the giant that preyed on Dushnikh Yal's herds. Chief Burguk named me Blood-Kin of the stronghold, and so of the Orcs.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.pitch: Then earn it. A giant has come down out of the hills and is stamping my goats flat for sport. Kill it, and bring Murbul something of it for her charms. Then we will talk about places.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.title: Blood-Kin
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.desc: The ancestral axe of Dushnikh Yal has been stolen, and Chief Burguk blames Chief Larak of Mor Khazgur. He wants the axe back, or blood-price paid.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o0.repl: The axe of my line. Twelve chiefs carried it. Larak of Mor Khazgur has wanted it since we were boys. Go to his stronghold and tell him to give it back or pay the blood-price. I would go myself, but then there would be a war, and Murbul says we cannot afford one this winter.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o2.repl: Burguk would blame me for the snow. Forsworn raided us both the same week. They took my brother's shield and three of my hunters. The raiders came out of Bruca's Leap Redoubt. Go there if you want Burguk's axe. Bring back my brother's shield and I will call it even.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o2.topi: Burguk says you took his axe.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o3.text: Clear the Forsworn out of Bruca's Leap Redoubt
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o4.jour: The Briarheart had hung the Orc trophies from the roof of the redoubt: a shield, a helm, and an old iron axe notched along the haft.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o4.text: Kill the Briarheart who led the raids
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o5.text: Take back the axe of Dushnikh Yal
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o6.repl: Hm. So Larak is not a thief. Only ugly. What would you have me do now, Blood-Kin? You have earned an opinion.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o6.text: Return the axe to Chief Burguk
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o6.topi: Your axe. The Forsworn took it, not Larak. They hit Mor Khazgur too.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c0.l: Send Larak the shield I took back, and a gift of your own. End the feud.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c0.r: A gift. To Larak. Murbul will laugh at me for a month. ...Fine. Peace is cheaper than war, and the Forsworn are the real enemy.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c1.l: You accused him in front of your clan. Pay him the blood-price for the insult.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c1.r: Blood-price, from me, to him. That is the Code, and you are right. I will pay. It will hurt more than any axe.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.outro: The Forsworn, not Mor Khazgur, stole the axe of Dushnikh Yal. I took it back from Bruca's Leap Redoubt, and on my advice Chief Burguk settled things with Chief Larak instead of starting a war.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.title: The Blood-Price
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.de: Murbul, wise-woman of Dushnikh Yal, sent me to the shrine of Malacath in Wrothgar to learn the meaning of the god's Code.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o0: Travel to the shrine of Malacath in Wrothgar
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o1: Two ogres were using the shrine's offering bowl as a cooking pot. Malacath, I suspect, found that funnier than I did.
Drive the ogres away from the shrine
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o2: I did not hear a voice. I heard the wind, and the fire, and my own breathing. And then, somehow, I understood that I had been told not to kneel.
Kneel before the shrine and listen
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o3: It always does, if you are not too proud to hear it, or too humble. Tell me, then. What did the Furious One teach you?
Return to Murbul at Dushnikh Yal
I went to Malacath's shrine. I think it told me something.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o4: That strength is something you carry for others.
Yes. A strong Orc alone is only a bandit. A strong Orc with a stronghold is a wall.
That nobody gives you a place. You take it.
That is how most of us learn it. Just remember that what you take, someone may take from you.
That he doesn't want to be begged. He wants to be proven right.
Ha! You heard him clearly. The cast-out god, proven right by the cast-out. That is the whole of it.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.ou: I knelt at Malacath's shrine in Wrothgar and came back with an answer. Murbul taught me the Code of Malacath and marked my brow with ash from her fire.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.pi: Blood-Kin who do not know the Code are guests with sharper teeth. Malacath is the god of the cast-out and the cursed, and his Code is how the cast-out live. Go to his shrine in Wrothgar, beyond the mountains, and listen. Then come back and tell me what you heard.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.desc: King Gurak means to honour me before the chiefs in the Hall of the Clans. Chief Bazrag gro-Fharun, who despises outsiders, has demanded the right to test me first, as the Code allows.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o0.re: Bazrag wants several words with you, and most of them are fists. He says no outsider should stand among the chiefs. The Code says he may test you. It does not say he must survive it, but I would rather he did. He has a good stronghold.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o0.to: I hear Bazrag wants a word with me.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o1.jo: Bazrag hit like a falling wall. When he finally went down to one knee, he spat out a tooth, laughed, and held out his hand.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o1.te: Beat Chief Bazrag gro-Fharun in the ring
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o2.re: He did, and now he says you are the best fight he has had in ten years. Stand there. The chiefs are watching, and I have something to say.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o2.te: Stand before the chiefs in the Hall of the Clans
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.outro: I beat Chief Bazrag gro-Fharun in the ring, and King Gurak named me an Honored Chief of the Orsimer before every stronghold in Wrothgar.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.title: Honored Chief
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.de: King Gurak is rebuilding Orsinium's walls. He wants the keystone of the old gate recovered from the ruins of Old Orsinium, and stone enough to set it.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o0: Travel to the ruins of Old Orsinium
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o1: Drive the ogre clan from the ruins
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o2: Thurga had made a throne of the old gate's stones and was sitting on the keystone itself. She did not take kindly to being asked to stand.
Kill the ogre matriarch, Thurga Stone-Chewer
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o3: Recover the keystone of the old gate
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o4: Older than my grandfather's grandfather, and still square. Good. Now the masons need stone to bed it in. Bring cut stone to the Forgemaster; she is keeping the tally.
Bring the keystone to King Gurak
The keystone of the old gate, my king.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o5: Thirty-two, all square. The masons will set the keystone at dawn. Stay and watch, Blood-Kin. You will want to say you were there.
Bring thirty-two stone bricks to Forgemaster Ghamrash
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.of: Forgemaster Ghamrash says you're rebuilding the walls.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.ou: I recovered the keystone of Old Orsinium's gate from an ogre clan and brought stone to set it in. The new gate of Orsinium stands on the bones of the old.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.pi: Every time Orsinium has fallen, we have built it again from its own bones. The keystone of the old gate lies in the ruins of Old Orsinium, and an ogre clan squats on it. Bring me that stone, and enough cut stone to set it in, and the new gate will carry the old one's name.
story.skycraft.q.orc_the_forgemasters_or: Word of my deeds has reached Orsinium. Forgemaster Ghamrash gra-Shura of the Hall of the Clans has sent for me: the city's forges are starving for orichalc.

I did. The orichalc seam at Coldperch Cavern feeds half the forges in this city, and a pack of durzogs has moved into the workings and eaten two of my miners. The King wants walls. Walls want steel. Steel wants ore. You see the problem.
Speak with Forgemaster Ghamrash in the Hall of the Clans
The durzogs had denned in the deepest gallery, among the miners' abandoned picks. The pack-mother was the size of a pony and twice as bad-tempered.
Kill the durzogs infesting the mine
Bring up a load of orichalc ore
Green right through. Good ore, better miner. I'll have the crews back down there by morning. Here: I made this from the last of the old stock. Orsinium steel for an Orsinium friend.
Bring the ore to Forgemaster Ghamrash
The mine is clear. Here's the first of the ore.
I cleared the durzogs from Coldperch Cavern and brought orichalc ore back for Forgemaster Ghamrash. The forges of Orsinium are burning again.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.desc: The Root Hist of Black Marsh is blighted and robbed by sap-thieves. Deeja-Sleeps of Stormhold wants pure sap saved before the tree sickens.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o0.text: Find the Root Hist in the deep marsh
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o1.text: Drive off the sap-thieves and the blighted beasts
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o2.text: Gather pure sap from the Root Hist
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o3.reply: The Hist will heal. And it will remember you. When an Argonian says that, walker, it is not a small thing.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o3.topic: Pure sap from the Root Hist.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.pitch: A blight. It creeps up the roots of the Root Hist in the deep marsh, and sap-thieves bleed the trees while they are weak. Go to the Root Hist. Bring back sap that is still pure.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.title: The Hist Remembers
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.desc: An Oblivion gate has opened above Kvatch, echoing the Crisis that once burned the city. Savlian Matius of the city watch needs someone to go through it and close it.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o0.text: Go to the Oblivion gate above Kvatch
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o1.text: Kill the dremora guarding the gate
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o3.text: Climb the Great Sigil Tower and defeat the Sigil Keeper
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o4.text: Take the Sigil Stone from its flame to close the gate
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o5.repl: Closed. Just like the Hero of Kvatch did it, two hundred years ago. Kvatch owes you, and Kvatch pays its debts.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o5.text: Bring the Sigil Stone to Savlian Matius
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o5.topi: The gate is closed. Here's what held it open.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.pitch: A gate. In the hills. Two hundred years after the Crisis, an Oblivion gate is open again above Kvatch. Somebody has to close it before what's behind it comes through.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.title: Echoes of Kvatch
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.desc: Dark spirits haunt the Temple of the Two Moons. Moon-Priest Azadhi asked me to cleanse it by moonlight and carry word to the Mane.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o0.text: Travel to the Temple of the Two Moons
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o1.text: Wait for the moons to rise
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o4.reply: The Mane felt it, the moment the light returned. You are not of the moons, and yet you served them. Elsweyr remembers its friends.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o4.text: Present the Lattice offering to the Mane in Riverhold
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o4.topic: The moons dance again over the temple.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.pitch: The Temple of the Two Moons has been desecrated by the Dro-m'Athra, the lost spirits. The Lunar Lattice cannot hold the moons' light while they haunt it. Cleanse the temple by night, when the moons can see you.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.title: Moons and Mane
story.skycraft.q.prov_ham_sword_singer.d: Yasmin at-Sentinel offered to test me in the way of the Yokudan sword-singers: claim an ancestral blade from the Ra Gada tomb and win a duel at Hel Ra Citadel.
story.skycraft.q.prov_ham_sword_singer.o: Travel to the Tomb of the Ra Gada
Lay the tomb's restless guardians to rest
Defeat the rival ansei in a duel
Then your blade sang, and you heard it. Keep it. A shehai is never given, only earned, and you have earned this one.
How does one become a sword-singer?
story.skycraft.q.prov_ham_sword_singer.p: You don't, not in one lifetime. But you can earn a shehai. Go to the tomb of the Ra Gada, the first warriors who sailed from Yokuda. Take an ancestor's blade, if its guardians let you. Then a rival waits at Hel Ra.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.desc: King Gurak gro-Morkul of Orsinium tests outsiders who would be friends of the Orcs: feed the forges, then kill the ogre of Wrothgar Peak.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o0.tex: Bring ten iron ingots for Orsinium's forges
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o3.tex: Kill the ogre of Wrothgar Peak
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o4.rep: Then the clans will sing of a pink-skin who climbed Wrothgar. Badly, but they'll sing. Orsinium's gates are open to you, blood-kin.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o4.tex: Bring the ogre's tusk to King Gurak
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.pitch: Iron, for the forges. And a monster dead, for the clans to see. Bring ten bars of iron to the stronghold forge, then climb Wrothgar Peak and kill the ogre that eats our goats.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.title: Orsinium Rising
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.de: Something is stirring in Red Mountain again. The Temple of the Tribunal wants the Great Houses' cooperation and someone to go into the heart of the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o0: Help costs. But a quiet mountain is good for trade. Hlaalu will open the roads. Tell the Temple we expect a discount on blessings.
Win House Hlaalu's support in Balmora
The Temple asks for Hlaalu's help on Red Mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o1: Redoran has been on Red Mountain for a thousand years. Go through the Ghostfence; our wardens will hold the gate behind you.
Win House Redoran's support in Ald'ruhn
The Temple needs Redoran on Red Mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o3: Fight through the ash creatures of Red Mountain
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o5: Quiet for now. The Temple will keep this shard where no Sleeper can find it. You have the gratitude of the Tribunal, and of all three Houses, which is rarer.
Bring the shard to Tharen Veloth in Vivec
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.pi: Red Mountain. Ash storms, and in the storms, voices. Sleepers walk out of the ash in Balmora and Ald'ruhn. The Great Houses argue; the Temple must act. Speak with Hlaalu and Redoran, and then go to the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.desc: A magister of Alinor says that recovering a stolen shard of the Crystal Tower might earn the attention of the Psijic Order, whose island of Artaeum appears only to those it chooses.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o3.text: Sail to Artaeum, which is suddenly on the horizon
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o4.repl: And so Artaeum let you land. Stay a while. The Order teaches nothing quickly.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o4.text: Give the shard to Celinar of the Psijic Order
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o4.topi: I've brought the Crystal Tower's shard.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.offer: I've heard Artaeum can't be found.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.pitch: It can't. Unless the Psijic Order wants you. Maormer raiders stole a shard of the Crystal Tower; return it, and perhaps the Order will notice you. Perhaps.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.title: Isle of the Psijics
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.desc: Spinner Aerfin of Elden Root wants me to live by the Green Pact, the Bosmer covenant with their forest, and bring a graht-oak seed out of the thorn-choked Green Heart.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.o0.t: Hunt three beasts, as the Pact allows
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.o4.r: Then the Pact is in you, whatever your ears look like. We'll plant it in Falinesti's old ground. One day it'll walk.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.o4.t: Bring the seed to Spinner Aerfin
The Wilderking gave me the seed.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.offe: Tell me about the Green Pact.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.pitc: Better: live it. Hunt as we hunt; take only flesh. Then go to the Green Heart, where thorns choke the old trees. The Wilderking guards a seed there. If the Pact is in you, he'll give it.
story.skycraft.q.ps_breaches_in_time.des: Ritemaster Iachesis sent me to close breaches in time that have opened on Summerset and Auridon. Daedra are crawling through them.
Find the time breach outside Firsthold
Inside the breach, a moment kept repeating: the same gull, diving into the same wave, over and over. When the last Dremora fell, the gull finally caught its fish.
Drive back the Daedra pouring through the breach
Find the second breach outside Alinor
Valzhar laughed as he died. He said the breach was not his doing, only his invitation.
Slay the Dremora holding the breach open
Collect a shard of the collapsed breach
Was he. Then the shard will tell us by whom. Look at the raindrops in it. Each one is a moment that did not happen. Someone is fishing for one of them.
Bring the shard to Ritemaster Iachesis
Both breaches are closed. One of the Dremora said he was invited.
story.skycraft.q.ps_breaches_in_time.out: I closed two breaches in time and brought Iachesis a shard of one. The Dremora who held it claimed someone had opened the way on purpose.
story.skycraft.q.ps_breaches_in_time.pit: Hands, and something sturdy attached to them. Tears are opening across Summerset, places where time has split and something has slipped in through the crack. Daedra, mostly. Close two for me, one near Firsthold and one outside Alinor. Bring me a shard.
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.desc: Loremaster Celarus sent me to Ceporah Tower, the ancient Psijic tower on Artaeum's cliffs, to face the trials every member of the Order has faced.
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.o1.jo: The tower did not speak in words. It just grew quieter and quieter until I could hear my own doubts, one at a time.
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.o1.te: Sit in silence on the first floor until the tower speaks
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.o2.te: Overcome the constructs of the second floor
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.o3.jo: The Warden did not attack until I did. I wonder now whether I had to fight it at all.
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.o3.te: Face the Warden of the Summit
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.o4.re: You came down. That is the passing. The Warden would have let you by, if you had thought to ask. Most never do. Remember that, Initiate.
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.o4.to: I climbed the tower. Did I pass?
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.outro: I faced the trials of Ceporah Tower. Celarus says the last of them could have been passed without a blow, and I am still thinking about that.
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.pitch: Climb. Ceporah Tower stands on the western cliffs, and every Psijic has climbed it. Each floor tests a thing you think you are. Some come down different. A few come down quickly. Go when you are ready, which is now.
story.skycraft.q.ps_ceporah_trials.title: The Ceporah Trials
story.skycraft.q.ps_isle_in_the_mist.des: For nights on end I dreamed of a fogbound island and a tolling bell. Magister Indaenir in Alinor told me it was a summons from the Psijic Order on Artaeum.
Sail west to the isle of Artaeum
Yes, that is generally how it goes. Keep the pearl; it was your invitation. Loremaster Celarus decides who stays. I only decide who gets lost on the way to him.
Speak with the Psijic waiting on the shore
I was dreaming of this place. Then I was here.
I decide very little. The Order decided before you dreamed your first dream of us. But a pearl is only an invitation. Tell me why you came.
Show the Mist-Pearl to Loremaster Celarus
Celinar says you decide who stays.
To learn what the Mages Guild cannot teach.
Honest, and a little arrogant. The Guild teaches magic as a tool. We teach it as a conversation. You will find we argue back.
Because the dream would not let me sleep.
Also honest. The Old Ways are not a choice so much as an itch. Welcome, Novice. Scratch carefully.
story.skycraft.q.ps_isle_in_the_mist.off: I keep dreaming of an island wrapped in fog.
story.skycraft.q.ps_isle_in_the_mist.out: Artaeum let itself be found. Loremaster Celarus accepted me into the Psijic Order as a Novice, the first outsider in a long while.
story.skycraft.q.ps_isle_in_the_mist.pit: Then you are either mad or summoned, and I have met you, so I doubt you are mad. The Psijic Order calls people that way. Sail west, to where Artaeum ought to be, and if the isle wishes to be found, it will be.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.desc: The breach shard pointed Iachesis to the Horologe of Kirenn, a Psijic instrument lost centuries ago. Sea Viper raiders from Pyandonea have found it in the ruins of Sunhold and are using it to tear holes in time.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o0.repl: A name. The Horologe of Kirenn, made by one of us before the Order left the world the first time. It measures the distance between what is and what might have been. In the wrong hands it shortens that distance. Maormer hands are very wrong. They hold Sunhold.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o0.text: Speak with Iachesis about the shard
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o0.topi: What did the shard tell you?
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o1.text: Travel to the ruins of Sunhold on Summerset
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o2.text: Break the Sea Viper hold on Sunhold
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o3.jour: Sirathel wanted a moment in which Pyandonea had won the war against Summerset. She was close to finding it. The Horologe was warm in her hands when she fell.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o3.text: Defeat the Maormer tidecaller who wields the Horologe
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o5.repl: Kirenn's own work. I have read about this instrument since I was younger than you. Keep it a moment longer. Before it goes back to the vaults, you must understand what it measures.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o5.text: Bring the Horologe to Loremaster Celarus on Artaeum
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.o5.topi: The Maormer had it. They won't need it now.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.outro: I took the Horologe of Kirenn back from a Maormer tidecaller in the ruins of Sunhold. Celarus wants me to understand it before it is locked away.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_horologe.title: The Horologe of Kirenn
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.desc: Celarus has agreed to teach me the Old Ways, the Psijic understanding of magic as a dialogue with the world rather than a command given to it.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o0.repl: No one is. Listen. The Mages Guild says: I will make fire. The Old Ways say: there is fire here already, waiting to be asked. The difference sounds small. It is the width of the world.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o1.c0.l: Then magic is listening, more than speaking.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o1.c0.r: Yes. And a mage who only speaks will one day be answered by something he did not expect.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o1.c1.l: Then magic has a will of its own.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o1.c1.r: Not a will. A shape. Water has no will, but it has a shape it prefers. Learn the shape and you need never force it.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o2.text: Go to the meditation stones below Ceporah Tower
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o3.text: Wait for the stars to rise over Artaeum
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o4.jour: The echo cast every spell I know, louder than I cast them, and never once paused to see what the world answered. That was how I beat it.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o4.text: Confront the echo of the mage you might have been
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o5.repl: The one who does not listen. Everyone meets theirs. Fewer get back up. You are an Adept of the Old Ways now, which means you have learned enough to know how little you know.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.o5.topi: I met someone at the stones. Myself, more or less.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.outro: Celarus taught me the first of the Old Ways. Beneath Ceporah Tower, under the stars, I faced the mage I would have become without them.
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_old_ways.title: The Old Ways
story.skycraft.q.ps_the_ritemasters_rite: The Horologe has been used too many times. A breach has opened above Artaeum itself, and Iachesis must perform an old rite to close it while someone holds back what comes through.
Yes. Sirathel tugged at the threads too often, and they have unravelled here, where the Order's own past is thickest. I need the Horologe and I need time to work. You will give me the second one.
The sky over the isle is torn.
Hold back the Daedra while Iachesis works the rite
Ulvathar fought in three moments at once, his blade landing before it swung. I learned to strike where he would be rather than where he was.
Slay the Markynaz who strides through the breach

In the vaults, where it will sleep until someone foolish wakes it again. Probably one of us. Take these, Loremaster. The circlet is old. The ones who wore it before you were not always wise, but they always listened.
The breach is closed. Is the Horologe safe?
Iachesis closed the breach over Artaeum while I held back the Daedra. The Council named me Loremaster of the Psijic Order, and one day, Iachesis says, I may stand where she stood.
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.desc: A Hlaalu swordsman named Ravos Andarys has been mocking Redoran honor in Ald'ruhn's taverns. Today he threw his glove at my feet. Redoran custom says a challenge must be answered.
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.o0.rep: Ravos Andarys. He has been begging for this for a month. A formal duel, outside the gate, before witnesses. Win, and the House's name is clean.
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.o0.tex: Show the challenger's glove to Neminda
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.o0.top: A Hlaalu threw this at my feet.
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.o1.jou: Ravos Andarys fought well and talked better. The witnesses carried him off afterwards, and no one in Ald'ruhn has mocked Redoran honor since.
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.o1.tex: Defeat Ravos Andarys in a formal duel
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.o2.rep: I watched. Clean and correct. Councilor Sarethi watched too. He wants to see you.
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.outro: I won a formal duel against the Hlaalu braggart Ravos Andarys. Councilor Athyn Sarethi has taken an interest in me.
story.skycraft.q.rd_duel_of_honor.title: A Duel of Honor
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.desc: Councilor Athyn Sarethi granted me a charter to build Indarys Manor, a Redoran stronghold at Bal Isra, northwest of Ald'ruhn.
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.o1.tex: Clear the kagouti and alit from the building site
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.o2.jou: Redoran masons build the way Redoran soldiers fight: without fuss, without rest, and in perfectly straight lines.
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.o2.tex: Wait while Redoran masons raise the first walls
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.o3.rep: Then Redoran has a new stronghold, and you have a seat to defend. There is one thing more I must ask of you, and it is not for the House. It is for my son.
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.o3.tex: Return the sealed charter to Athyn Sarethi
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.o3.top: Indarys Manor's walls stand at Bal Isra.
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.offer: Neminda said you wished to see me, Councilor.
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.outro: The walls of Indarys Manor stand at Bal Isra. Councilor Sarethi has a personal favour to ask.
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.pitch: The Hlaalu are building strongholds in the west, and the Telvanni in the east. Redoran must answer. Take this charter to Bal Isra and raise Indarys Manor. It will be yours to hold for the House.
story.skycraft.q.rd_indarys_manor.title: Indarys Manor
Varvur Sarethi, the Councilor's son, stands accused of murder. His father swears he is innocent. I mean to find the truth before the Council passes sentence.
I found the body. That's all. A man in a grey hood ran from the alley, east, toward the old grotto by the river bed. I told the guards. They didn't write it down.
Your father asked me to help. What happened?
Deal with the cutthroats hiding in the grotto
Kill the real murderer, Ervyn Faryon
A single letter. V. Thank you. You have given me back my son.
Bring the proof to Athyn Sarethi
The man who framed Varvur was paid for it. Look at the signature.
I proved Varvur Sarethi innocent of murder. The man who framed him was paid by someone signing as 'V', and Councilor Sarethi believes it was Archmaster Venim.
story.skycraft.q.rd_trapped_in_shulk.des: The kwama in Shulk Egg Mine have turned on their miners, and ash creatures have followed them up from the deep tunnels. Neminda sent me to rescue a trapped miner, Dulnea Ralaal.
Ash spawn in an egg mine. They don't belong this far from the mountain. Something is stirring under Vvardenfell.
Walk? I can run, if you go first. Get me to Ald'ruhn and I'll never complain about the ash again.
House Redoran sent me. Can you walk?
Ash spawn. I'll tell the Council. You did well. A miner alive is worth more to the House than a mine full of eggs.
Dulnea is safe. There were ash spawn in the mine.
story.skycraft.q.rd_trapped_in_shulk.off: Is there work for a hireling?
story.skycraft.q.rd_trapped_in_shulk.out: I rescued Dulnea Ralaal from Shulk Egg Mine. The ash spawn I found there worry Neminda more than she shows.
story.skycraft.q.rd_trapped_in_shulk.pit: Shulk Egg Mine, east of the city. The kwama have turned on the miners, and something else came up from the deep tunnels with them. One miner is still inside. Bring her out.
story.skycraft.q.rd_venims_challenge.des: Athyn Sarethi has named me challenger to Archmaster Bolvyn Venim. By Redoran law, the Archmaster must answer a formal challenge on the duelling floor.
A hireling with borrowed honor. Very well. The old law gives you the right to die on the duelling floor. I'll grant it gladly.
Sarethi has named me your challenger.
Defeat Archmaster Bolvyn Venim in the duel
It is. Venim's pride was his undoing. Yours, I hope, will be tempered by duty. Archmaster.
story.skycraft.q.rd_venims_challenge.out: I defeated Bolvyn Venim in a formal duel and became Archmaster of House Redoran.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.desc: Neminda of the Redoran Council Hall in Ald'ruhn will accept me into House Redoran if I prove I can do my duty: thin out the cliff racers harassing the caravan road, then report to the Warden.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.o1.re: Four fewer to dive at the carts. Good. Neminda will want to hear it from you, not me. Go.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.o1.te: Report to the Warden of Ald'ruhn
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.o1.to: Neminda sent me. The cliff racers on the caravan road are dead.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.o2.re: Then so am I. Kneel. You are a hireling of House Redoran. Remember: your actions are the House's actions now, for good or ill.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.offer: I want to serve House Redoran.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.outro: I joined House Redoran in Ald'ruhn. The House values duty over glory, and I mean to learn what that costs.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.pitch: Then serve. Cliff racers have been diving at our caravans on the Ald'ruhn road and the guards can't keep up. Kill four of them, then report to the Warden. A Redoran does the work in front of them without asking whether it's beneath them.
story.skycraft.q.rd_weight_of_duty.title: The Weight of Duty
story.skycraft.q.rk_breaking_the_stockad: The Thalmor keep a stockade outside Rimmen where they hold Khajiit accused of rebellion. Most were never rebels. Shazrah wants them freed, starting with a farmer named Ra'khaj.

The Dominion stockade. Elves in gold armour keeping Khajiit in pens on Khajiit land, with Ri'Vasha's blessing. There is a farmer there, Ra'khaj. His village asked for him. Bring him home, and break as many locks as you can on the way.
You said you had something bigger.
Lorenwe had a list of every prisoner and the crime he had invented for each. I kept it. Shazrah will want to read it aloud.
Kill the Justiciar who runs the stockade
This one can run, if you let him. Every other pen is open now. Listen to them go.
Your village sent for you. Can you walk?
Bring Ra'khaj to the hidden camp
Then tonight a dozen villages have their sons back, and the Thalmor have one less Justiciar. Sit, farmer.
The stockade is empty. Ra'khaj is here.
I broke open the Dominion stockade outside Rimmen, killed its Justiciar, and brought the farmer Ra'khaj back to the Renrijra camp. Every pen in the stockade stands empty.
story.skycraft.q.rk_laughter_in_the_dune: Warlord Shazrah, who leads the Renrijra Krin from a hidden camp outside Rimmen, wants me to rob an Anequinan noble's tax-collector before she will trust me.
Intercept the tax-collector east of Rimmen
The collector dropped his reins and ran as soon as the first guard fell. He was, as Shazrah said, only a clerk.
Good. Half goes back to the villages it came from, quietly, at night. Half buys arrows. That is the whole philosophy of the Renrijra Krin. Welcome, Recruit.
I want to fight beside the Renrijra Krin.
I robbed an Anequinan tax-collector for Warlord Shazrah. Half of the coin goes back to the farmers, half to the fight. I am a Recruit of the Renrijra Krin.

Everyone wants to fight beside us until they see how we eat. A noble's tax-collector rides east of Rimmen today with a chest of farmers' coin. Take it. Leave the collector alive if you like; he is only a clerk. Bring the chest here.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.desc: The Renrijra Krin need weapons, and the smugglers of Senchal have them. Shazrah has sent me to make an arrangement with a smuggler named Dar'jazad.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o1.r: Steel is easy. Getting it past the Thalmor customs post outside the city is hard. Dar'jazad will sell you the steel. You will get it past the customs post. And then we talk about what else Dar'jazad might ship for the Krin.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o1.t: Shazrah sent me. She needs steel.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o2.c: Steel only. The Krin don't move skooma.
Hmph. Principles. Expensive, principles. Fine. Steel only, at a higher price.
Ship what you like through our country. We'll take a cut.
Now that is a partnership. The skooma will flow, the coin will flow, and nobody will ask where the Krin's arrows came from.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o2.t: Settle the terms of the alliance
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o4.t: Collect the crate of smuggled steel
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o5.r: Pickled fish. Ha. Good. I will not ask what you promised him. One day the bill will come, and we will pay it then.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o5.t: Senchal steel, and an arrangement with Dar'jazad.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.outr: I struck a bargain with the Senchal smuggler Dar'jazad and brought a crate of steel back past the Thalmor customs post. The Renrijra Krin are armed, and indebted.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.desc: Lord Ri'Vasha, the Anequinan noble who sells his own people's grain and sons to the Thalmor, has a Thalmor guard at his estate west of Rimmen. Shazrah means to end him, and she wants me at the head of the attack.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o0.re: Ri'Vasha's estate. He has Thalmor at his gate and Thalmor gold in his vault. Go in first. When he falls, the rest of his house will fall with him.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o0.to: We're armed. Where do we strike?
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o1.te: Lead the attack on Ri'Vasha's estate
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o3.jo: Ri'Vasha told me the Renrijra were thieves who would starve Anequina within a year. He may even have believed it. He died in a room full of grain.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o4.re: Servants, cooks, a steward, a few cousins. Some fed the Thalmor. Most only fed Ri'Vasha. The band is waiting on your word.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o4.to: Ri'Vasha is dead. What of his household?
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o5.c0: Open the granary to the villages. Let the servants go.
A Laughing Blade who feeds people. The priests will not know what to say about you.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o5.c1: Burn it. Let every noble in Anequina smell the smoke.
Fear is a weapon too. They will smell it in Riverhold. They may not forgive us for it.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.outro: I led the Renrijra Krin against Lord Ri'Vasha's estate and killed him among his Thalmor guards. Warlord Shazrah named me a Laughing Blade.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.title: The Last Laugh
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.desc: Shazrah sent me to take Lord Ri'Vasha's sugar tithe from a caravan on the road outside Rimmen. The guards serve the noble; the traders only drive his wagons.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o0.te: Find the caravan on the road outside Rimmen
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o2.re: Rawan-dar has a wife in Rimmen and two kits who think he sells silk. Please. Take the sugar. Take the silk, too. Only let us go.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o2.to: The guards are dead. That leaves you.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o3.c0: Take the sugar. Go home to your kits.
The moons see you. Rawan-dar will tell no one which way you went. He will not even tell himself.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o3.c1: No witnesses. Shazrah's rule, not mine.
Rawan-dar understands. He does not forgive, but he understands.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o5.re: Good. Whatever you did on that road, you did it, not me. That is how it works here. Each of us carries our own weight.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.outro: I took Lord Ri'Vasha's sugar tithe from his caravan. What became of the traders was my own choice, and Shazrah made sure I knew it.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.pitch: A caravan carries Lord Ri'Vasha's sugar tithe south of the city. The guards are his. The traders are not; they are hired, and poor, and frightened. What you do with them is your business. The sugar is mine.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.title: The Spice Road
story.skycraft.q.sh_krev_the_skinner.des: Krev the Skinner leads the Silver Hand from the ruined fort of Gallows Rock. Brenna Ashfall wants him stopped before he takes revenge for Greymoor.
Fight through the Silver Hand at Gallows Rock
Krev talked the whole fight: about beasts, about blood, about the pelts he would hang in his hall. He stopped talking at the end.
Then the Silver Hand have lost their knife. But a knife needs a hand to hold it. Krev took orders from someone. I want to know who.
story.skycraft.q.sh_krev_the_skinner.out: I killed Krev the Skinner at Gallows Rock. Brenna Ashfall believes someone above Krev still holds the Silver Hand together.
story.skycraft.q.sh_silver_under_greymoo: The list was written at Fort Greymoor, a Silver Hand hideout west of Whiterun. Njada Stonearm of the Companions went there to settle it alone and has not come back.
Fight through the Silver Hand in the fort
Hrafnhild kept a branding iron shaped like a silver hand heating in the brazier. Njada was chained beside it, and had not yet been marked.
Kill Hrafnhild Silver-Brand, the fort's warden
I can stand, walk and hit things. A Vigilant's errand-runner, saving a Companion? Don't tell Vilkas. Get me out of here and I'll owe you a drink, maybe two.
Good. Whatever the Companions are, they did not deserve that. Hrafnhild answered to Krev the Skinner. He holds Gallows Rock, and he will know by now what we did.
Greymoor is ours. Njada is home in Jorrvaskr.
I cleared the Silver Hand from Fort Greymoor and brought Njada Stonearm of the Companions home alive. Their warden answered to Krev the Skinner of Gallows Rock.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.desc: With Krev the Skinner dead, the Silver Hand in Skyrim answer to one man: Varek Silverfist. Brenna Ashfall has word of a courier carrying his orders on the road north of Whiterun.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o0.r: Krev was the knife. Varek Silverfist is the hand that holds it, and nobody has seen his face in years. A courier rides for him on the road north of the city. Take what he carries.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o0.t: Krev is dead. Is it over?
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o1.t: Stop Varek's courier on the north road
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o3.r: Arrogant enough to write it all down. He gathers the last of them at Driftshade Refuge, north in the Pale. I'm coming with you. Njada says she is too, and I have stopped arguing with her.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o3.t: Bring Varek's journal to Vigilant Ashfall
The courier was carrying Varek's own journal.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o5.j: They kept a werewolf in chains to train their recruits, starved half to madness. When the chains broke, it went for the hunters first.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o5.t: Break the Silver Hand's last stronghold
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o6.j: Varek wore a gauntlet of real silver, his whole right hand. He swore the beasts would inherit Skyrim without him. Then he fell, and the gauntlet rang on the stone.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o7.r: In Skyrim, at least. Take this. It was Varek's, and it has hunted too many innocent people. Let it hunt something that deserves it.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.outr: I took Varek Silverfist's journal from his courier and followed it to Driftshade Refuge, where I killed him and broke the last of the Silver Hand in Skyrim.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.de: Vigilant Brenna Ashfall believes the Silver Hand, a band of self-styled werewolf hunters, murdered a pelt-trader at Chillfurrow Farm because he did business with the Companions.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.o0: He sold wolf pelts to Jorrvaskr for twenty years. That's all. They came at night with silver arrows and said he was 'feeding the beasts.' They camp in the gully east of here. I can still hear them laughing.
Speak with Sigrun at Chillfurrow Farm
Vigilant Ashfall sent me. I'm sorry about your husband.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.o1: The stalkers had a fire going and Sigrun's furs drying beside it. One of them was wearing her husband's boots.
Clear the Silver Hand camp east of the farm
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.o3: Bring the list to Vigilant Ashfall in Whiterun
The Silver Hand were carrying this. It's a list of names.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.of: You look like someone who's lost a trail.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.ou: The Silver Hand murdered a pelt-trader for selling furs to the Companions, and they carry a list of others marked to die. Vigilant Brenna Ashfall means to end them.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.pi: Not lost. Followed it too far. The Silver Hand murdered a pelt-trader at Chillfurrow Farm because he sold furs to the Companions. They call it hunting werewolves. I call it butchery, and I mean to prove it. Will you help?
story.skycraft.q.sol_ash_spawn.desc: Raven Rock is attacked by ash spawn, creatures of ash that walk out of the wastes.
story.skycraft.q.sol_ash_spawn.o0.text: Destroy the ash spawn at Raven Rock's wall
story.skycraft.q.sol_ash_spawn.o1.reply: For now is more than we usually get. The Council sends its thanks. And so does my bar tab.
story.skycraft.q.sol_ash_spawn.o1.topic: The ash spawn are gone, for now.
story.skycraft.q.sol_ash_spawn.pitch: Ash spawn. They crawl out of the ash itself and walk on the wall. The Redoran Guard can't hold them every night. Help them, and the Council will pay.
story.skycraft.q.sol_ash_spawn.title: March of the Dead
story.skycraft.q.sol_cleansing_the_stone: The Skaal shaman Storn says Miraak is using the All-Maker's stones to bend Solstheim to his will. Each must be cleansed with my Voice.
The All-Maker's stones: Wind, Sun, Water, Beast, Tree. Miraak has poisoned them all. Your Voice cleansed the Earth Stone; cleanse the others, and he loses his grip on my people.
Speak with Storn in the Skaal village
I feel it. The wind is ours again. But Miraak drew his power from a Black Book. To face him you'll need one too. Neloth, the Telvanni wizard, collects such things.
story.skycraft.q.sol_dragonborn.desc: Masked cultists attacked me on the road, calling me a false Dragonborn. Their orders mention a place called Solstheim and a man named Miraak.
story.skycraft.q.sol_dragonborn.o2.reply: Miraak? No. But half the town wakes up every morning with blisters on their hands and no memory of the night. They walk out to the old stone by the shore and build something. You might look at that.
story.skycraft.q.sol_dragonborn.o2.text: Ask about Miraak in Raven Rock
story.skycraft.q.sol_dragonborn.o2.topic: Have you heard of someone called Miraak?
story.skycraft.q.sol_dragonborn.title: Dragonborn
story.skycraft.q.sol_path_of_knowledge.d: Neloth knows of a Black Book in Nchardak, a Dwemer ruin in the east of Solstheim. Reading it may show me how Miraak learned his power.
story.skycraft.q.sol_path_of_knowledge.o: Naturally. There is one in Nchardak, behind a great many Dwemer puzzles and a great many Dwemer machines. Fetch it. Don't read it on my floor.
Speak with Neloth at Tel Mithryn
Take the Black Book from Nchardak
Inside the Black Book, Hermaeus Mora granted me a word of a Shout that bends the will of others. Miraak learned it here, long ago.
Find the Black Book that closes the chapter and read your way out
story.skycraft.q.sol_summit_of_apocrypha: Storn read the Black Book Waking Dreams, and gave his life to show me the way to Miraak. It is time to face the first Dragonborn.
Read Waking Dreams at the Temple of Miraak
Fight Miraak's dragon on the Summit of Apocrypha
Read the Black Book on the Summit to return to Solstheim
story.skycraft.q.sol_temple_of_miraak.de: The people of Raven Rock sleepwalk to an old standing stone and build a shrine around it. The Earth Stone. My Voice might break whatever holds them.
story.skycraft.q.sol_temple_of_miraak.o1: Free the Earth Stone with Unrelenting Force
story.skycraft.q.sol_temple_of_miraak.o2: Travel to the Temple of Miraak
story.skycraft.q.sol_temple_of_miraak.o3: Fight through the Temple of Miraak
story.skycraft.q.sol_temple_of_miraak.o5: Miraak. The first Dragonborn. He's been gone for millennia and he's not gone at all. Come to my village. Our shaman will know what to do.
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.desc: Two Shadowscales have died on contracts this month, ambushed by killers who knew exactly where they would be. Elder Sees-Behind-Eyes thinks someone inside the enclave is selling us.
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.o0.re: Our contracts are being sold. I do not know by whom. You are new, so you are the only one I am sure it is not. Watch the others. Start with the ones who smile.
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.o1.re: Bad luck, little one. It happens. Contracts go wrong. Now if you'll excuse me, I have an errand in Helstrom. Nothing interesting.
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.o1.to: Two of us died this month. Any thoughts?
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.o3.te: Fight off the Morag Tong agents at the meeting
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.o4.jo: Weighs-the-Coin had a purse of Morag Tong gold on his belt. It was heavier than I expected. I wonder if that was how much we were each worth to him.
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.o6.te: Bring the writ to the Elder
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.o6.to: It was Weighs-the-Coin. He sold every name in the enclave to the Morag Tong.
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.outro: I followed Weighs-the-Coin to Helstrom, where he was selling Shadowscale names to the Morag Tong, and killed him. The writ he carried named every one of us.
story.skycraft.q.ss_a_scale_turned.title: A Scale Turned
story.skycraft.q.ss_born_under_the_shado: Elder Sees-Behind-Eyes of the Shadowscale enclave outside Stormhold told me I was born under the sign of the Shadow. To prove it, I must kill a Dunmer slaver camped east of the city.
Find the slavers' camp east of Stormhold
Dreleth had four of our people chained to a stake. When he was dead I cut them loose, and they ran into the reeds without a word. That was thanks enough.
And you came back with his iron instead of his purse. Good. The Shadow chose well. You are a Hatchling of the Shadowscales now. Do not let it go to your tail.
Bring the branding iron to Sees-Behind-Eyes
The slaver is dead. His captives are free.
You say I hatched under the Shadow?
I killed a Dunmer slaver outside Stormhold and freed his captives. Elder Sees-Behind-Eyes took me into the Shadowscales.

Every Saxhleel born under that sign belongs to the Shadowscales, whether they know it or not. Most are found as hatchlings. You were missed. A Dunmer slaver is camped east of the city, branding our people. Show me what the Shadow made you.
story.skycraft.q.ss_speaker_of_shadows.d: The Morag Tong did not take the loss of their informant quietly. Their killers are coming for the enclave outside Stormhold, and the Elder means to meet them in the mud.
story.skycraft.q.ss_speaker_of_shadows.o: Tonight. They think we are scattered and grieving. We are neither. Take the eastern approach; they will come that way, because it is the dry one, and dry-skins love dry ground.
I heard the Tong is coming.
Wait for nightfall at the enclave
Hold the eastern approach against the Morag Tong
Indoril fought like a priest at prayer, every stroke in its proper place. The marsh had no proper places. He slipped, once, and that was enough.
Then all of the enclave is alive because of you. Stand here, in the middle, where everyone can see.
The eastern approach held. Their master is dead.
I held the eastern approach against the Morag Tong and killed their Exalted Master. Elder Sees-Behind-Eyes named me a Shadowscale and the one who will one day speak for the Shadow.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.desc: Hatcheries in Murkmire are being robbed. The eggs are sold to collectors in Cyrodiil who keep Argonian hatchlings as curiosities. The Elder has given the contract to me.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.o1.rep: Six clutches in one season. The thief is one of us, a Lukiul who wears Imperial clothes and calls himself a merchant. He hides in Xal Irasotl, the old pyramid in the drowned forest. Bring our eggs home.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.o1.top: The Shadowscales sent me about the stolen eggs.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.o2.tex: Find the xanmeer of Xal Irasotl
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.o4.jou: Hixeeh said he was only a merchant, and that the collectors would have found someone else. He was right about the second part. Now the collectors will have to.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.o6.rep: Still warm. Oh, still warm. They will hatch knowing the marsh and not some Imperial's glass cage. When they are old enough, I will tell them a Shadow brought them home.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.o6.tex: Bring the eggs home to Tah-Weesh
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.outro: I tracked a Lukiul egg-thief to the xanmeer of Xal Irasotl in Murkmire, killed him, and brought a clutch of stolen eggs back to their hatchery.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_egg_thief.title: The Egg-Thief of Murkmire
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_kings_contract.d: Teeba-Enoo, envoy of the King of Argonia, gave me my first royal contract: an Imperial magistrate near Gideon who still holds Argonians in debt-bondage, years after the Empire withdrew.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_kings_contract.o: Find the magistrate's plantation outside Gideon
Deal with the plantation's hired guards
Calidius had a ledger of debts going back twenty years, each one paid many times over. I burned it with him.
So I see. The King will melt this down and have it made into something useful. A spoon, perhaps. You will hear from him again, Shadow-Hatched.
Bring the seal to Teeba-Enoo in Stormhold
The Elder says you carry a list.
I fulfilled the King of Argonia's contract on Magistrate Calidius near Gideon and brought his seal back to Teeba-Enoo.
story.skycraft.q.ss_the_kings_contract.p: A short one. One name. An Imperial magistrate stayed in Gideon after the Empire left, kept his seal, and still collects 'debts' from our people on his plantation. The King would like the debts cancelled. Permanently. Bring the seal as proof.
story.skycraft.q.ss_what_the_hist_teache: Deeja-Sleeps sent me to drink the sap of an ancient Hist and dream. Every Shadowscale is taught by the Hist before they are taught by anyone else.
Drink the sap and sleep beneath the Hist
In the dream it was always behind me. I stopped running and stood still in the dark, and then it was in front of me, and then it was gone.
Hunt the thing that hunts you in the dream
Yes. The Hist teaches the Shadow-born that stillness is a weapon. What did it mean to you?
Something hunted me. I stopped running, and it came to me.
That patience kills more surely than speed.
The answer of a good Shadowscale. The Elder will be pleased.
That fear is only a hunter I haven't faced yet.
The answer of a brave one. Brave Shadowscales are rare. Try to stay rare by staying alive.
The Elder says the Hist must see me.
I drank from an ancient Hist and dreamed of being hunted until I stopped running. Deeja-Sleeps says the Hist has taught me what it teaches all the Shadow-born.

The Elder is right. A Shadowscale's blade is sharpened by steel, but its hand is taught by the Hist. Go to the old root-tree south of here, drink, and sleep. What you dream is the lesson. Do not be afraid of what hunts you there.
story.skycraft.q.tg_blindsighted.desc: Mercer Frey is after the Eyes of the Falmer, the great gems of the Dwemer ruin Irkngthand. That's where we'll catch him.
story.skycraft.q.tg_blindsighted.o1.text: Fight through the Falmer of Irkngthand
story.skycraft.q.tg_blindsighted.o3.repl: Then there's one thing left. The Key goes home to the Twilight Sepulcher. Keep the gems; the Guild needs them more than Nocturnal does.
story.skycraft.q.tg_blindsighted.o3.topi: Mercer is dead. I have the Key.
story.skycraft.q.tg_blindsighted.title: Blindsighted
story.skycraft.q.tg_chance_arrangement.d: Brynjolf, a fast talker in Riften's market, offered me work for coin: steal something unnoticed, then meet him in the Ragged Flagon under the city.
story.skycraft.q.tg_chance_arrangement.o: Steal something in Riften without being caught
Find the Ragged Flagon in the Ratway
Clean work. Welcome to the Thieves Guild, then. Mercer Frey runs things here, but you'll deal with me. First, we have a few debts to collect.
What kind of work are you offering?
story.skycraft.q.tg_chance_arrangement.p: Something a bit shady. Lift a ring from a market stall and plant it on a merchant. Do it clean, and there's more where that came from. Meet me in the Ragged Flagon after.
story.skycraft.q.tg_dampened_spirits.des: Honningbrew Meadery is cutting into the Black-Briar mead trade, and whoever bought Goldenglow is behind it. Maven wants Honningbrew ruined at its own tasting.
Problem? An infestation! Clear out the basement and I'll pay you. Here, put this bane on the nests. Careful, it's strong.
Talk to Sabjorn at Honningbrew Meadery
I hear you have a skeever problem.
Clear the skeevers from the meadery cellar
Captain of the guard tastes it at the opening, Sabjorn hangs, Honningbrew is mine. You have a future, thief.
Sabjorn's 'pest poison' is something else entirely.
story.skycraft.q.tg_darkness_returns.des: The Skeleton Key must be returned to the Ebonmere in the Twilight Sepulcher, Nocturnal's temple. Only then will the Guild's luck return.
Return the Skeleton Key to the Ebonmere
I can feel it already: the coin's flowing again. The Guild needs a Guild Master, and nobody's earned it like you.
Return to Brynjolf in the Ragged Flagon
It's done. The Key is home.
story.skycraft.q.tg_loud_and_clear.desc: The owner of Goldenglow Estate, the honey farm on the lake, has stopped paying the Guild. Maven Black-Briar, our best client, wants the estate hurt badly, and wants to know who's backing its owner.
story.skycraft.q.tg_loud_and_clear.o2.jo: Inside the safe was a bill of sale. Someone else bought Goldenglow, and signed it with a mark: a stylized sun.
story.skycraft.q.tg_loud_and_clear.o3.re: A buyer with a sun for a signature... Honningbrew Meadery has the same mark on its barrels. That's next. Maven will be pleased.
story.skycraft.q.tg_loud_and_clear.o3.te: Bring the bill of sale to Brynjolf
story.skycraft.q.tg_loud_and_clear.title: Loud and Clear
story.skycraft.q.tg_scoundrels_folly.des: The sun mark belongs to a rival, and the trail leads to Snow Veil Sanctum, where a Guild traitor named Karliah may be hiding. Mercer Frey wants her dead.
Karliah. She murdered our last Guild Master, Gallus, twenty-five years ago. Now she's back. She's hiding in Snow Veil Sanctum. You're coming with me.
Brynjolf says you have a job for me.
Meet Mercer at Snow Veil Sanctum
Mercer said that? Mercer shot you in the back a moment ago. Look at the wound. Then listen to me.
Mercer... the vault! He's emptied the vault! Go with Karliah. I'll hold the Guild together. Find him.
Mercer's been robbing the Guild blind. Gallus wrote it down.
story.skycraft.q.tg_taking_care_of_busin: Brynjolf wants three of Riften's merchants reminded that they owe the Guild: Keerava, Bersi Honey-Hand and Haelga.
Tell Brynjolf he will have it. And tell him to stop sending strangers to my bar.
Not the urn! Fine, fine. Here. Take it and get out.
You owe the Guild. Pay up, or the pottery pays.
Dibella forgive me, I meant to pay. Here. And not a word about the... visitors to my bunkhouse.
Brynjolf sent me about your debt.
That's the way. Next job is bigger: Maven Black-Briar wants the Goldenglow Estate taught a lesson.
story.skycraft.q.tg_trinity_restored.des: Karliah was a Nightingale, one of three agents sworn to the Daedric Prince Nocturnal. To catch Mercer we need Nocturnal's favor, and the Nightingale armor waiting in Nightingale Hall.
Then stand on the circle. Don't speak until she does.
Take the Nightingale oath with Karliah
story.skycraft.q.tgc_count_of_anvil.desc: Corvus Umbranox is going home to Anvil and to the wife who waited for him. Before he goes, he asked me to carry his family ring to Countess Millona, and to take up the Gray Cowl after him.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_count_of_anvil.o1.r: Thank you. Whoever you are. Thank you.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_count_of_anvil.o1.t: Give the Umbranox ring to Countess Millona
Countess. Someone asked me to return this to you.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_count_of_anvil.o2.r: Then the Gray Fox isn't gone at all, is he? Don't tell me your name. I'll forget it anyway. Welcome back, Fox.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_count_of_anvil.o2.t: The Gray Fox is gone home. He left me the cowl.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_count_of_anvil.outr: Corvus Umbranox is home in Anvil. I wear the Gray Cowl now, and the Thieves Guild of Cyrodiil answers to the Gray Fox, as it always has.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_magistrates_ring.de: Word came through the Waterfront that S'krivva, the Guild's doyen in Bravil, has a job for a fresh pair of hands: a magistrate who fines beggars for sleeping in the rain has a gold ring she'd like to see change owners.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_magistrates_ring.o1: Yes. The magistrate keeps his seal ring in a box by his bed, because he trusts no one. He is right not to. His house is on the north side, beside the canal. Bring the ring, and touch no one.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_magistrates_ring.o2: Steal the magistrate's ring from his house
story.skycraft.q.tgc_magistrates_ring.o3: Good. Now he will have to beg for a new seal, and the clerks will make him wait a very long time. This one is pleased. The fence pays well for gold like this.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_magistrates_ring.ou: I stole a Bravil magistrate's seal ring for S'krivva. The beggars of Bravil, I'm told, had a very good week.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.desc: With the Ayleid map, I am to climb from the Imperial Substructure into the White-Gold Tower and steal an Elder Scroll from the Imperial Library, without killing anyone.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.o0.tex: Enter the deep passages of the substructure
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.o1.tex: Deal with what waits in the deep passages
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.o2.jou: I came up through a seam in the floor of the Library, under the noses of the Palace guard. Nobody saw me. Nobody bled.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.o2.tex: Steal the Elder Scroll from the White-Gold Tower
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.o3.rep: No one ever will, either. Stand back. I've waited a long time for this.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.o3.tex: Bring the Elder Scroll to the Gray Fox
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.o3.top: The Scroll. And no one saw me take it.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.outro: I stole an Elder Scroll from the White-Gold Tower. The Gray Fox read it, and the world remembered his true name: Corvus Umbranox, the lost Count of Anvil.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_scroll_heist.title: Theft of the Elder Scroll
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.desc: The Gray Fox himself has asked to meet me in the Waterfront hideout. He wants help with a theft that has never been attempted: an Elder Scroll from the Imperial Library, and a way in that the Palace guard knows nothing about.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.o0.re: I did. The Elder Scrolls can rewrite what the world remembers. With one, I can be free of this cowl's curse. The way in is under the city, through Ayleid halls older than the Tower they hold up.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.o1.te: Find a way into the Imperial Substructure
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.o2.te: Get past the old guardians of the substructure
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.o3.te: Recover the map of the Ayleid passages
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.o4.re: Better than I hoped. Rest tonight. Tomorrow we steal from the Emperor himself, and no one is going to get hurt doing it.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.o4.te: Bring the map to the Gray Fox
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.o4.to: The passages run right under the White-Gold Tower.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.outro: The Gray Fox showed me his face, briefly, and told me about the cowl. Beneath the Imperial City there is a road into the White-Gold Tower, and I have the map.
story.skycraft.q.tgc_the_gray_cowl.title: The Gray Cowl
story.skycraft.q.tgc_watch_captains_list: Captain Hieronymus Lex of the Imperial Watch is planning raids on the Guild's fences. Armand Christophe wants me to steal Lex's raid roster from the Watch office and warn the Guild before the gates close.
Lex's office was tidy to the point of obsession. The roster lay squared to the edge of his desk, with a dagger laid across it as a paperweight.
Steal the raid roster from the Watch office
Slip out of the Imperial City before the Watch seals the gates
Then he will find empty rooms and cold hearths. Our people move tonight. This one will see Armand hears of this, and the Gray Fox after him.
Bring the roster to S'krivva in Bravil
Lex's raid list. Every fence he knows about.
Lie low while the raids come up empty
Lex's raids found nothing but empty rooms. The Guild knows who to thank, and so, I suspect, does the Gray Fox.

It should. Captain Hieronymus Lex of the Watch has decided the Gray Fox is a personal insult. He's planning raids on our fences and safehouses, and he keeps the list in his office. Get that list, warn S'krivva, and get out of the city before he locks the gates.
Armand Christophe, the doyen of the Thieves Guild on the Imperial City Waterfront, will let me try out for the Guild. I need to steal something and pick a pocket without getting caught.
Steal two things without being caught
Light enough. Rules, then: we don't kill, we don't steal from the poor, and we don't steal from each other. Break any of those and the Gray Fox will hear of it. Welcome to the Guild.
Return to Armand Christophe on the Waterfront
I hear there's a guild down here that isn't on any charter.
I passed Armand Christophe's tryouts and joined the Thieves Guild of Cyrodiil, which answers to the Gray Fox.

Could be. Could be it's a story the Watch tells to justify its budget. If you want to find out, take something that isn't yours in this city, and lift a purse without anyone feeling it go. Then come back and we'll talk like friends.
story.skycraft.q.th_a_question_of_heresy: Elenwen sent me to Rorikstead to investigate Talos worship. A farmer named Sigrun Frost-Hand is said to keep a hidden shrine. I am beginning to wonder what the Thalmor do with such people afterwards.
Told by whom? We grow grain. My father fought at the Red Ring for the Empire you made peace with. If there's a shrine, it's his, and he's dead.
Question Sigrun Frost-Hand in Rorikstead
I'm told there is a shrine to Talos nearby.
Warn her: the Justiciars will come. Get your family away tonight.
Why would one of you... No. Don't explain. Thank you. We'll be gone by dark. There are some at the shrine who won't leave. I can't help them.
Tell her the Dominion is merciful to those who cooperate.
Merciful. I've heard what that word means in your mouths. Do what you came to do, then.
Decide what to tell her
Find the hidden shrine outside Rorikstead
They died with the god's name in their mouths. I told myself it was the law. It was easier to believe in the middle of the fight than afterwards.
Talos Zealot
Desperate Worshipper
Deal with those defending the shrine
Take the amulet from the altar
And the family? No, never mind. The Nords keep running and we keep finding them. Your report will say the shrine was destroyed. Leave the rest of it to me.
Bring the amulet to Elenwen
The shrine is gone. This was on the altar.
Do you have more work for me?
