I destroyed a shrine to Talos outside Rorikstead and brought its amulet to Elenwen. Whatever I told Sigrun Frost-Hand, I will carry it for a long time.

A small thing. A farming family near Rorikstead keeps a shrine to Talos in their barn. The worship of a man as a god is a lie the Concordat forbids. Speak to them. Find the shrine. Bring me what you find on the altar.
A Question of Heresy
story.skycraft.q.th_eyes_of_the_dominion: Justiciar Erunor Vaelanwe in Alinor offered me a test: find the treasonous letter someone has been leaving beneath a stone on the city's quay, and bring it to him without reading it.
Find the letter under the loose cobblestone
The courier drew a knife when he saw me standing over his stone. He was not a fighter, only a man paid to walk somewhere at night.
Deal with the courier who comes to collect it
You did not. I would have known. The courier will not be missed, and his employer will be found. Welcome to the Thalmor, Agent. You begin in Skyrim.
Bring the letter to Justiciar Vaelanwe
The letter. I did not read it.
I wish to serve the Thalmor.
I passed Justiciar Vaelanwe's test in Alinor and was taken into the Thalmor as an Agent. My first posting is the embassy in Skyrim.
Many do, in words. Someone in Alinor is leaving letters for the enemies of the Dominion under a cobblestone on the quay. Find the letter, bring it to me unread, and we will discuss your future.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.desc: First Emissary Elenwen sent me after a Blade who survived the Great War and has hidden as a hunter in the hills above Falkreath ever since.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.o1.te: Get past the hunter's guard dogs
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.o2.jo: He was old and slow and still very nearly killed me. At the end he said only that the dragon would return whether the Thalmor liked it or not.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.o4.re: One fewer. They are like weeds: cut one and three more were already seeding somewhere. Still. The Dominion remembers who does the cutting.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.o4.te: Bring the insignia to Elenwen at the embassy
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.o4.to: The Blade is dead. Here is his badge.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.offer: Justiciar Vaelanwe sent me to you.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.outro: I hunted down an old Blade in the hills above Falkreath and brought his insignia to First Emissary Elenwen.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.pitch: He told me you were punctual. Good. One of the old Emperor's Blades has been hiding in the hills above Falkreath for thirty years, living as a hunter. He was careless at a market last month and someone remembered his face. Bring me his insignia.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_last_blade.title: The Last Blade of Falkreath
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.desc: Elenwen is holding a reception at the embassy for Skyrim's nobility. Someone among the guests or the staff has been selling her letters to Windhelm, and she wants the traitor found before the evening ends.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.o0.rep: I did. Smile, take a cup, and listen.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.o1.rep: Fourteen years in this frozen province. I know which jarl drinks, which one gambles, and which one owes money to the other. Knowledge is the only currency that never freezes.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.o1.top: You seem to know everyone here.
And who buys your knowledge, Envoy?
Buys? What a curious word. Excuse me. I see the Emissary's steward waving.
Flatter him and let him keep talking.
You are a wise one. Most new agents preach. You listen. Come to my study some evening. We could help each other.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.o4.tex: Search the study for his correspondence
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.o5.rep: Telanil. Fourteen years and a seat at my table. He left the moment you walked out of the hall, of course. A ship for Summerset was waiting. Justiciar Vaelanwe will want to hear this himself.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.o5.top: It's Orvanwe. He's been selling your notes to a buyer in Windhelm.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.outro: At Elenwen's reception I found the traitor: Envoy Telanil Orvanwe, who had been selling the embassy's secrets to Ulfric's people. He fled to Summerset before he could be taken.
story.skycraft.q.th_the_reception.title: An Evening at the Embassy
story.skycraft.q.th_traitor_in_gold.desc: Telanil Orvanwe has fled to his family's estate on Summerset, outside Alinor. Justiciar Vaelanwe wants him brought to the Dominion's justice, and he wants me to be the one who brings it.
story.skycraft.q.th_traitor_in_gold.o0.r: To his family estate west of the city. He has hired swords, and he thinks old blood will shield him. It will not. Go, and come back with the matter closed.
story.skycraft.q.th_traitor_in_gold.o0.t: Report to Justiciar Vaelanwe in Alinor
Orvanwe is a traitor. He has fled home.
story.skycraft.q.th_traitor_in_gold.o3.j: He offered me half of what Ulfric paid him. Then all of it. Then he drew his sword, and that was the only honest thing he did all night.
story.skycraft.q.th_traitor_in_gold.o4.r: Then the matter is closed, and you closed it. Stand still a moment. There is a letter from the Emissary, and I am to read it in front of you.
story.skycraft.q.th_traitor_in_gold.o4.t: It's done. Orvanwe will sell nothing more.
story.skycraft.q.th_traitor_in_gold.outr: I ended Telanil Orvanwe's treason at his family estate on Summerset. Justiciar Vaelanwe read out Elenwen's letter: I am a High Justiciar of the Thalmor.
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.desc: The blight has reached Suran. The apothecary Sedrisa Vandu is out of remedies, and the Temple has sent me to help her.
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.o1.r: Then help me fast. I need ash salts and trama root, and both grow out past the old guar track where the kagouti den. Bring me a good bundle.
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.o1.t: The Temple sent me to help with the blight.
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.o2.t: Clear the kagouti from the herb grounds
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.o3.t: Gather ash salts and trama root
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.o4.r: Enough for every bed in the village. Sit with them while it brews. Prayers help, and so does a hand to hold.
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.o4.t: Bring the ingredients to Sedrisa Vandu
Ash salts and trama root. As much as I could carry.
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.o5.j: Through the night, the coughing quieted, bed by bed. Brother Dranos of the village chapel worked beside us without a word about the Temple.
story.skycraft.q.tt_blight_of_suran.outr: I helped cure Suran of the blight. Brother Dranos Velas worked beside me, and I learned later that the Ordinators are watching him.
story.skycraft.q.tt_ghostgate_vigil.desc: Sixth House cultists are marching on the pilgrims' shrine beside the Ghostgate. The Buoyant Armigers are stretched thin, and Archcanon Saryoni has asked me to hold the shrine.
story.skycraft.q.tt_ghostgate_vigil.o0.t: Reach the shrine at the Ghostgate
story.skycraft.q.tt_ghostgate_vigil.o1.t: Hold the shrine against the Dagoth cultists
story.skycraft.q.tt_ghostgate_vigil.o2.t: Kill the cult's leader, the Ash Prophet
story.skycraft.q.tt_ghostgate_vigil.o3.r: Then the pilgrims will walk there tomorrow, and never know how close it came. Stay. I have one more thing to say, and I want to say it in the Fane.
story.skycraft.q.tt_ghostgate_vigil.o3.t: The shrine at the Ghostgate stands.
story.skycraft.q.tt_ghostgate_vigil.outr: I held the Ghostgate shrine against the Sixth House. Archcanon Tholer Saryoni raised me to Patriarch of the Tribunal Temple.
The Ordinator Tharen Veloth has asked me to investigate Brother Dranos Velas of Suran, suspected of writing heretical tracts against the Tribunal.
Search Brother Dranos's chapel for his writings
Then you know I don't hate the Three. I only ask what they are, and where they've gone. If that is heresy, the Temple is more fragile than it thinks.
I'll take this to the Ordinators. The law is the law.
Then I'll pack. Thank you for letting me say it to your face, at least.
Burn it. Keep tending your sick, and keep your questions quiet.
Mercy, from a Temple servant. Perhaps I was wrong about the Temple after all.
And made your choice, I see. The Temple asks for judgment from its servants, not only obedience. You'll need both where you're going.
Report to Tharen Veloth in Vivec
You wanted to speak with me, Ordinator?
I investigated Brother Dranos Velas for heresy and decided what the Ordinators would hear.
You were in Suran. So was Brother Dranos Velas, who writes tracts doubting the Three. Find his writings and bring them to me. What happens to him then is the Temple's business. And yours, I suspect.
story.skycraft.q.tt_pilgrimage_of_graces: Canon Dalvilu Arethan of the Balmora temple sent me on the Pilgrimage of the Seven Graces, to pray at the shrines of Kummu, Koal Cave and the Ghostgate, then present myself to Archcanon Tholer Saryoni in Vivec.
At the Fields of Kummu I knelt in the mud as the pilgrims do, in memory of Vivec helping a farmer carry his load. My knees are still wet.
Pray at the shrine in the Fields of Kummu
Pray at the shrine of courage in Koal Cave
Pray at the shrine of valor beside the Ghostgate
So I see. Your token is full and your boots are worn through. Welcome to the Tribunal Temple, Layman. Walk with the Three.
Present your pilgrim's token to Archcanon Saryoni in Vivec
I have walked the Graces, Archcanon.
I want to serve the Tribunal Temple.
I walked the Pilgrimage of the Seven Graces and was received into the Tribunal Temple by Archcanon Tholer Saryoni.

Every servant of the Temple walks the pilgrimage of the Graces. Pray at the Fields of Kummu for humility, at Koal Cave for courage, and at the Ghostgate for valor, then present your token to the Archcanon in Vivec. Walk it with an open heart.
The Pilgrimage of the Seven Graces
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.desc: Balmora citizens have been lured away by dreams to Ilunibi, a cave held by the Sixth House. Canon Arethan has asked me to cleanse it.
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.o1.tex: Destroy the ash creatures and dreamers
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.o2.jou: Dagoth Odros came apart into hot ash. The chanting stopped. Two dreamers in the lowest chamber woke and asked me where they were.
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.o2.tex: Destroy the ash vampire Dagoth Odros
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.o3.rep: An ash vampire, so close to Balmora. The Sixth House grows bolder. The Temple owes you its thanks, and the dreamers owe you their minds.
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.o3.top: Ilunibi is cleansed. An ash vampire led the dreamers.
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.offer: Is there work for the Temple, Canon?
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.outro: I purged Ilunibi of the Sixth House and destroyed the ash vampire Dagoth Odros.
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.pitch: Dreamers have been walking out of Balmora at night and not coming back. The Ordinators traced them to Ilunibi, a cave to the north. It belongs to the Sixth House now. Purge it.
story.skycraft.q.tt_purge_ilunibi.title: The Purging of Ilunibi
story.skycraft.q.tv_a_mouth_at_council.d: Master Aryon wants me to speak for him at the Telvanni Council as his Mouth. The masters will not listen without an endorsement from someone they fear, and no one frightens them like Divayth Fyr.
story.skycraft.q.tv_a_mouth_at_council.o: Does he? One of my experiments has walked out of its cell and is sulking in the lower hall. Put it back. Permanently is fine.
Ask Divayth Fyr for an endorsement
Master Aryon asks that you vouch for me before the Council.
It had been a storm atronach once. Fyr had changed something about it. I didn't ask.
Good. Take this to the Council. It says exactly what I think of you, which is more than I say of most.
Your experiment won't trouble you again.
'Not a fool.' Gods, he's never written that about me. Come. The Council is sitting.
Present the endorsement at the Council House
Propose that the House trade openly with the Empire.
Boldly done. Half of them hissed, which means they listened. Aryon looks delighted.
Insist that no Telvanni bends the knee to Imperial law.
They nodded. Even Gothren nodded. Aryon looks pained, but you won the room.
Speak for Master Aryon at the Council
I spoke for Master Aryon before the Telvanni Council as his Mouth, carrying Divayth Fyr's endorsement.
story.skycraft.q.tv_archmagister.desc: Archmagister Gothren has refused to recognize me as a master. Master Aryon says there is only one Telvanni answer: go to Tel Aruhn and take the seat.
story.skycraft.q.tv_archmagister.o1.repl: Recognise you? I'll have you made into a lamp. Guards!
story.skycraft.q.tv_archmagister.o1.topi: The Council will recognise me, Gothren, or it will need a new Archmagister.
story.skycraft.q.tv_archmagister.outro: I defeated Gothren at Tel Aruhn and took his seat. I am Archmagister of House Telvanni.
story.skycraft.q.tv_archmagister.title: Archmagister
story.skycraft.q.tv_by_telvanni_law.desc: Mistress Sedura Sarano, who bound daedra to the site of Tel Uvirith, has sent assassins after me since the Council session. By Telvanni law, a wizard may answer such an insult in kind.
story.skycraft.q.tv_by_telvanni_law.o0.r: Sedura Sarano. She wanted Uvirith and lost it to you. Telvanni law permits you to settle the matter at her tower. Few would blame you. Fewer would mourn her.
story.skycraft.q.tv_by_telvanni_law.o0.t: Ask Master Aryon about the attacks
Someone keeps sending assassins after me.
story.skycraft.q.tv_by_telvanni_law.o3.j: Sedura Sarano died believing I would never dare. In House Telvanni, that is the most common last thought.
story.skycraft.q.tv_by_telvanni_law.o4.r: Then you have done what every master of this House has done at least once. Now there is only one obstacle left between you and the Council's highest seat.
story.skycraft.q.tv_by_telvanni_law.o4.t: Sedura Sarano won't trouble me again.
story.skycraft.q.tv_by_telvanni_law.outr: By Telvanni law, I settled my quarrel with Mistress Sedura Sarano at her own tower.
Master Aryon has given me tower spores to grow my own Telvanni mushroom tower, Tel Uvirith, in the Molag Amur.
Travel to the site of Tel Uvirith
Someone had bound daedra to guard the site before I arrived. Feldras says that is a Telvanni's way of saying 'I was here first.'
Banish the daedra a rival wizard bound to the site
Fine spores. Healthy. Give me a day, and some quiet, and I'll show you something worth living in.
Give the spores to Feldras Morvayn
Master Aryon sent me with these spores.
By the next evening a pale stalk taller than three men stood where the spores went in, and Feldras was humming to it.
Is there work worthy of a Telvanni, Master Aryon?
Tel Uvirith has begun to grow in the Molag Amur. In a Telvanni's eyes, I am now someone with a house.

Every Telvanni of standing has a tower. You will need one, if you want anyone to take you seriously. There is a site in the Molag Amur called Uvirith. Take these spores, clear the ground, and find Feldras Morvayn. He grows the best towers in the House.
story.skycraft.q.tv_hirelings_errand.des: Mallam Ryon, who speaks for the masters at the Telvanni Council House in Sadrith Mora, will accept me as a hireling if I fetch a jar of fresh netch jelly for one of the masters.
Hunt a bull netch outside Sadrith Mora
Remarkable. You may call yourself a hireling of House Telvanni. Do not call yourself anything grander in front of a master. They are very easily bored, and boredom makes them creative.
Bring the netch jelly to Mallam Ryon
story.skycraft.q.tv_hirelings_errand.off: I want to join House Telvanni.
story.skycraft.q.tv_hirelings_errand.out: I joined House Telvanni as a hireling. The masters do not know my name yet. Mallam Ryon assures me this is a blessing.
story.skycraft.q.tv_hirelings_errand.pit: You and every other hopeful who can light a candle with a thought. Very well. A master requires jelly from a bull netch, fresh. Kill one, bring the jar, and do not drop it. The last hireling dropped it.
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.de: Mistress Dratha's raw glass contract with the Zebabi mine has been undercut by a Hlaalu agent. She wants her glass, and she wants the agent to regret it.
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.o0: Travel to the Zebabi glass mine
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.o1: Deal with the Hlaalu agent's hired guards
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.o2: The Hlaalu agent ran when his guards fell. He left the glass, a half-eaten lunch, and a contract worth three times what Dratha was paying.
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.o3: Hmph. Adequate. More than adequate. You may approach to within five paces from now on. Do not let it go to your head.
Bring the raw glass to Mistress Dratha
Your glass, Mistress. The Hlaalu agent won't be back.
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.of: Mallam Ryon says you have work, Mistress.
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.ou: I recovered Mistress Dratha's raw glass from the Zebabi mine. She allowed me to stand five paces closer, which I am told is unprecedented.
story.skycraft.q.tv_raw_glass_bargain.pi: I have a contract for raw glass from the Zebabi mine. The miners now say a Hlaalu agent has bought the lode out from under me. I want my glass, and I want the agent to understand what it means to cheat a Telvanni.
story.skycraft.q.und_last_one_standing.d: Glirion the Redbeard, who keeps the Undaunted enclave in Daggerfall, invited me to join his band of delvers. His idea of an interview is a drinking contest followed by a spider nest.
story.skycraft.q.und_last_one_standing.o: That's the spirit. Mind the third one, it bites back.
Drain the last tankard and slam it down.
Ha! Upright and smug about it. I like you already. Go and sleep it off on the road north.
Quietly pour the last one into his potted fern.
That fern has been drunk since the Interregnum. You think I didn't see? Clever is good in a dungeon. Go on, then.
Find the spider cave called Spindleclutch
The broodmother had wrapped three shepherds and a mule in her silk. I didn't look too closely at what was left.
Clear the spiders out of Spindleclutch
Pull a fang from the Broodmother
Look at the size of it! That goes on the wall, and you go in the book. Welcome to the Undaunted. First round's on you next time.
Bring the fang to Glirion in Daggerfall
One fang, as requested. The nest is empty.
I hear the Undaunted take anyone who can survive a dungeon.
I outlasted Glirion the Redbeard at the table, or near enough, and cleared Spindleclutch for him. The Undaunted wrote my name in their book.
story.skycraft.q.und_last_one_standing.p: Anyone who can survive a dungeon and a drinking contest, in that order or the other. Drink with me first. If you're still on your feet, there's a spider nest north of town that's been eating shepherds, and I need a fang off the mother.
story.skycraft.q.und_legendary_delve.des: Glirion, Maj and Urgarlag have one last delve none of them ever finished: the deepest hall of Labyrinthian in Skyrim, once called Bromjunaar, where an ancient warden still keeps the horn that called the Nords to war.
Labyrinthian. The old city of Bromjunaar. Every one of us has tried its lowest hall and every one of us came back carried. There's a warden down there with a horn, and there's an empty peg on our wall. Fill it.
Maj says you've been saving something.
Fight through the halls of Bromjunaar
The Warden blew his horn once as I came in. Every draugr in the hall answered. When he finally fell, the echo kept going for a long time.
By all the gods and a few of the princes. Maj! Urgarlag! Get in here, and bring the good cask.
Bring the horn home to the Daggerfall enclave
Your peg's been empty long enough.
story.skycraft.q.und_legendary_delve.out: I finished the delve no Undaunted had finished: the lowest hall of Labyrinthian. The Warden's horn hangs on the enclave wall in Daggerfall, and my name is carved beneath it.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.desc: Glirion gave me my first Undaunted pledge: delve Bleak Falls Barrow in Skyrim and take the torc of the draugr king who still rules its lowest hall.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.o0.te: Travel to Bleak Falls Barrow in Skyrim
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.o1.te: Fight through the barrow's restless dead
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.o2.jo: The Barrow-King spoke one word as he rose. I didn't know it, but my ears rang for an hour afterwards.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.o2.te: Defeat the Barrow-King on his throne
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.o4.re: Cold, isn't it? Nordic iron never forgets what it was made for. One pledge down. Maj in Wayrest has the next, and she's in a mood, so bring your manners.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.o4.to: The Barrow-King won't need this anymore.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.outro: I fulfilled my first pledge in Bleak Falls Barrow and brought the Barrow-King's torc back to Daggerfall.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.pitch: A promise to walk into a place everyone else walks away from. Your first is in Skyrim: Bleak Falls Barrow, above Riverwood. The Nords buried a king up there and he hasn't stopped sitting on his throne. Bring me his torc.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_barrow.title: Pledge: The Barrow-King
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.desc: Urgarlag Chief-bane in Mournhold pledged me to the Dreloth Ancestral Tomb, a Velothi crypt where a grave-robber has stirred up the dead and stolen a funeral mask.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.o0.t: Find the Dreloth Ancestral Tomb outside Mournhold
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.o1.t: Lay the angry ancestors back to rest
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.o2.j: Fendyn had a sack of grave goods and a very poor understanding of what the Dunmer do to people who rob their dead. The dead got to him before I did, almost.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.o4.r: Good. Now the interesting part. The Undaunted keep trophies. The Dreloths want their mask. Nobody will ever know which you chose, except you.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.o4.t: The tomb is quiet. I have the mask.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.o5.c: The mask goes back to the Dreloth family.
Hm. I'd have done the same, and then lied about it at the table. I'll see it's returned with your name attached.
It's a trophy. I earned it.
Ha. Glirion will love it. Just don't wear it to Mournhold's temple, and don't sleep with it under your pillow.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.o5.t: Decide what becomes of the mask
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.offe: Maj sent me. She says you're the fun one.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.outr: I put the Dreloth ancestors back to sleep and killed the man who woke them. Urgarlag let me decide what to do with the stolen mask, and I decided.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_dreloth.pitc: She's lying, I'm the honest one. A grave-robber broke into the Dreloth family tomb outside Mournhold and woke up everything inside it. The Dunmer want their ancestors put back to sleep, and they want their mask back. Pledge accepted?
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.desc: Maj al-Ragath in Wayrest pledged me to the Ayleid ruin of Garlas Malatar in Cyrodiil, where necromancers are draining the old starlight from its stones.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.o0.t: Travel to Garlas Malatar in Cyrodiil
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.o1.t: Purge the necromancers and their thralls from the ruin
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.o2.j: Ilvas had chained himself to the Varla stone with silver wire, as if the light could keep him young. It couldn't.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.o2.t: Destroy the Light-Eater at the heart of the vault
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.o3.t: Take the Varla stone before it fades
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.o4.r: Well. Glirion owes me five drakes. I bet you'd come back with a dark rock and a sad face. Urgarlag has the next pledge in Mournhold. She'll like you. Try not to encourage her.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.o4.t: Bring the Varla stone to Maj al-Ragath in Wayrest
The stone's still lit. The thief isn't.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.offe: Glirion says you have a pledge for me.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.outr: I delved Garlas Malatar for Maj al-Ragath, ended a necromancer who was feeding on Ayleid starlight, and carried the Varla stone back to Wayrest still glowing.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_malatar.pitc: Garlas Malatar, in the Great Forest of Cyrodiil. The Ayleids built it to hold starlight, and something down there has been drinking it. Necromancers, most likely. Bring me the Varla stone from the lowest vault, and don't let it go dark.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_mazzatun.des: Urgarlag sent me into Black Marsh to climb the abandoned xanmeer of Mazzatun near Stormhold, where something large has made its nest, and bring back its sun-idol.
Travel to the Ruins of Mazzatun near Stormhold
Fight your way up the tiers of the xanmeer
Old Thunder-Jaw had been sleeping on the altar for so long that the stone had worn into the shape of its belly. The lightning in its throat lit the whole summit when it died.
Slay the old wamasu nesting at the summit
Take the sun-idol from the summit altar
That's a pretty thing. Ugly, but pretty. There's one more before Glirion's big one. Maj wanted the Dwemer job for herself, but she's busy shouting at someone in Wayrest. Go and see her.
The pyramid is yours. The wamasu is somebody's boots, eventually.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_mazzatun.out: I climbed the xanmeer of Mazzatun, killed the wamasu that ruled its summit, and brought its sun-idol back to Urgarlag.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_mazzatun.pit: Black Marsh. There's a xanmeer near Stormhold called Mazzatun, an old stepped pyramid the Argonians abandoned when their gods changed their minds. Something big nests on the top tier now. Bring back the sun-idol and we'll call it a pledge.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.de: Maj al-Ragath pledged me to Volenfell, a Dwemer city under the Alik'r Desert. Treasure-hunters reopened it and woke its machines.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.o0: Travel to Volenfell in the Alik'r Desert
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.o2: The Gate-Warden stood over the treasure-hunters' bodies, still guarding a door none of them had reached. When it fell, every machine in the city went still.
Bring down the Centurion guarding the core
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.o3: Take the gyro-core from the Centurion's cradle
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.o4: Still spinning. Dwemer work never knows when to quit. That's five pledges. Go to Daggerfall. Glirion has been saving something, and for once I think he's sober about it.
Bring the gyro-core to Maj al-Ragath in Wayrest
Volenfell is quiet again. Here is its heart.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.of: Urgarlag says you have a Dwemer ruin for me.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.ou: I shut down Volenfell's machines and brought its gyro-core to Maj al-Ragath. That was my fifth pledge: barrow, ruin, tomb, pyramid and Dwemer city.
story.skycraft.q.und_pledge_volenfell.pi: Volenfell, under the Alik'r sand. The Dwarves built it, my grandmother's people sealed it, and a band of fools has just unsealed it looking for gold. Their screams stopped a week ago. Go in, shut the machines down, and bring me the core that drives them.
story.skycraft.q.vg_ashes_of_the_hall.de: The Volkihar have stormed the Hall of the Vigilant. Keeper Carcette survived the first assault, but the vampire lord who led it is still inside.
story.skycraft.q.vg_ashes_of_the_hall.o0: Drive the Volkihar from the Hall
story.skycraft.q.vg_ashes_of_the_hall.o1: Vingalmo rose on leathery wings and called the dead Vigilants to their feet against me. When he fell, they lay down again, and I said Stendarr's prayer over each of them.
Destroy Vingalmo, lord of the Volkihar
story.skycraft.q.vg_ashes_of_the_hall.o2: What is left of it. Help me up. No, I'm all right; it's only a cut, and a great deal of grief. Stay a moment. There is something the Vigilants owe you.
Vingalmo is destroyed. The Hall is ours again.
story.skycraft.q.vg_ashes_of_the_hall.ou: I drove the Volkihar out of the Hall of the Vigilant and destroyed Vingalmo, the vampire lord who led them. Keeper Carcette named me Hand of Stendarr among the ashes.
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.desc: Keeper Carcette of the Vigilants of Stendarr sent me to take a Daedric relic from the cultists who dug it up beneath the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon.
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.o0.t: Travel to the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.o1.j: The cultists were chanting over a hole in the ground when I arrived. The scamps came out of the hole.
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.o1.t: Drive off the cultists at the shrine
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.o2.t: Take the relic the cultists unearthed
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.o3.r: A shard of a sigil stone. They would have opened a door with it, sooner or later. It goes into the vault, and you, if you still want it, go onto the rolls of the Vigilants. Welcome, Novice.
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.o3.t: Bring the relic to Keeper Carcette
The cultists are dead. This is what they dug up.
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.offe: I want to join the Vigilants of Stendarr.
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.outr: I took a fragment of a Daedric sigil stone from cultists at the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon. Keeper Carcette accepted me into the Vigilants of Stendarr.
story.skycraft.q.vg_stendarrs_vigil.pitc: Then let us see whether you can stomach the work. Cultists have been digging beneath the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon, south of here, and they have found something that should have stayed buried. Take it from them. Do not touch it more than you must.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.desc: Keeper Carcette sent me to Dawnstar to confiscate the Daedric curios that a dealer named Hestor Aldrinus has been selling to wealthy collectors.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o1.rep: Want them? They're art. History. And legal, mostly. What happens to my customers afterwards is between them and their nightmares.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o1.top: The Vigilants of Stendarr want your Daedric curios.
One of your customers hasn't stopped screaming in a week. The next one could be you.
...Take it. Take the whole box. I haven't slept well since that ring came in anyway.
This isn't a request. Hand it over.
Thugs in grey robes. Fine. Take it, and may it bite you.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o2.tex: Convince Aldrinus to give up the casket
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o3.jou: The lid of the casket came open on its own outside the town walls. I was glad I was not still standing in the shop when it did.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o3.tex: Deal with what crawls out of the casket
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o4.rep: It rarely does. I'll seal it tonight and see to it that nothing in this box ever reaches a rich man's mantelpiece again.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o4.tex: Bring the casket to Keeper Carcette
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.o4.top: Aldrinus's stock. Some of it didn't want to come.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.outro: I confiscated a casket of Daedric curios from Hestor Aldrinus in Dawnstar and fought off what escaped from it. Keeper Carcette has sealed it away.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.pitch: There is always more. A dealer in Dawnstar named Hestor Aldrinus buys and sells Daedric curios to rich fools in Solitude. One of his customers woke up screaming last week and has not stopped. Confiscate his stock, by persuasion if you can.
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_collector.title: The Collector of Dawnstar
story.skycraft.q.vg_the_harvesters_hollo: The Volkihar have allies: a cult of Molag Bal, the Harvester of Souls, who keep a shrine in a hollow north of the Hall and supply the vampires with captives. Keeper Carcette wants the shrine purged.
We take away their friends first. Molag Bal's faithful keep a shrine in a hollow north of here, and our scouts have seen them leading captives to it in chains. Free whoever you can. Purge the rest.
What do we do about the Volkihar?
Purge the cultists of Molag Bal
Ulvra died laughing. She told me the Hall was already burning, that the shrine had only been there to draw the Keeper's best away. I ran.
Kill the cult's high priest, Ulvra Chain-Keeper
Hurry back to the Hall of the Vigilant
I purged the cult of Molag Bal at the Harvester's Hollow, but it was a feint. While I was gone, the Volkihar attacked the Hall of the Vigilant.
story.skycraft.q.vg_under_the_broken_fan: Travellers have been vanishing on the road west of Whiterun. Keeper Carcette believes vampires have made a nest in Broken Fang Cave.
Three travellers gone in ten days near Broken Fang Cave, and a shepherd found drained in the snow. That is not wolves. Go, and take the sun with you if you can.
Hjalmar said he had a patron, and that his patron would avenge him. He laughed about it right up until the end.
Destroy the master of the nest
Volkihar wax. The old clan from the islands off Solitude. And they are counting our keepers. This was not a nest, it was a watch post. They are coming for the Hall.
Bring the missive to Keeper Carcette
The nest is gone. Their master was carrying this.
I purged a vampire nest in Broken Fang Cave. Its master carried orders from the Volkihar to watch the Hall of the Vigilant and count its keepers.
story.skycraft.scene.abduction.0: You fall asleep. You wake on the floor of a shack you've never seen, wrists free, door barred. Three hooded figures kneel, bound, along the wall.
story.skycraft.scene.abduction.1: Sleep well? You killed Grelod. A contract that was ours to take. Now you owe us a life. One of these three. Your choice.
story.skycraft.scene.ad_crystal_tower.0: Light pours down through the Crystal Tower, splitting into colours on the floor. Altmer, Bosmer and Khajiit stand side by side beneath it, and not all of them look comfortable.
story.skycraft.scene.ad_crystal_tower.1: My mother's court said this alliance could not last a season. It has lasted because people like this one carried it across Tamriel on foot.
story.skycraft.scene.ad_crystal_tower.2: Kneel, and rise as my Hand. When I cannot be there, you will be.
story.skycraft.scene.ad_crystal_tower.3: Raz will be weeping now, in a very dignified way. Do not look.
story.skycraft.scene.ad_veil_lifted.0: Lord Varandil. Raz has eaten at his table. He has excellent wine and very ugly opinions about cats.
story.skycraft.scene.ad_veil_lifted.1: The Veiled Heritance thinks the Queen shames Summerset by shaking hands with Bosmer and Khajiit. They would rather the Dominion die pure than live together.
story.skycraft.scene.ad_veil_lifted.2: They are wrong, and now they are also short one lord. Good work, friend.
story.skycraft.scene.alduin_dies.0: Zu'u unslaad! Zu'u nis oblaan... I am eternal... I cannot end...
story.skycraft.scene.alduin_dies.1: The World-Eater breaks apart into light, and his soul scatters across Sovngarde like sparks on the wind. Even the honored dead fall silent.
story.skycraft.scene.alduin_flees.0: Krosis... this is not over, joor. I will feast on the dead of Sovngarde and return stronger than ever.
story.skycraft.scene.alduin_flees.1: Alduin hurls himself into the clouds and is gone.
story.skycraft.scene.alduins_wall.0: There, in the center: Alduin himself, cast down. Not slain! Cast out, by the ancient tongues with a Shout of their own making.
story.skycraft.scene.alduins_wall.1: They called it Dragonrend. A Shout that forces a dragon to understand mortality. It is the only weapon the wall shows.
story.skycraft.scene.alduins_wall.2: Then the Greybeards must know it. They know everything about the Voice.
story.skycraft.scene.apocrypha.0: The Black Book opens in your hands and the world folds. Green sky. Black water. Towers of books, and tentacles where a horizon should be.
story.skycraft.scene.apocrypha.1: Another Dragonborn in my realm. How interesting. Miraak was my champion. Perhaps he still is. Prove otherwise.
story.skycraft.scene.ar_first_bout.0: Citizens of the Imperial City! Fresh meat for the sand today: a Pit Dog with no name, no record, and no idea what's coming!
story.skycraft.scene.ar_first_bout.1: The gate grinds up. The crowd roars. Across the sand, your opponent spits and lifts a notched blade.
story.skycraft.scene.ar_grand_champion.0: The Gray Prince falls to one knee on the sand. He looks up once, at the stands, and nods, as if the noise is something he finally understands.
story.skycraft.scene.ar_grand_champion.1: The Gray Prince has fallen! Citizens, I give you your new Grand Champion!
story.skycraft.scene.ar_gray_prince.0: My father was a lord of Cyrodiil. That's what my mother told me, before she died. Not that he was this.
story.skycraft.scene.ar_gray_prince.1: A vampire. And my mother, gods, she must have been his... no. I won't say it. Every title I've won, every crowd that chanted my name, they were cheering for that.
story.skycraft.scene.ar_gray_prince.2: I can't stand in that Arena and pretend any more. When we fight, champion, do not hold back. I want to go down honestly, if I go down at all.
story.skycraft.scene.artaeum.0: Artaeum appears to those the Order has need of. Sit. Breathe. Listen to the old ways. When you leave, you will see magic differently.
story.skycraft.scene.ash_ashkhan.0: You came to us an outlander. You hunted with us, honored our wise woman, made peace with the Erabenimsun and brought our ancestors home.
story.skycraft.scene.ash_ashkhan.1: The clan has spoken by the fire. When I am gone, they would follow you. Until then, sit beside me. You are Ashkhan in all but the title.
story.skycraft.scene.ash_ashkhan.2: The ancestors are laughing again. This time, I think they are pleased.
story.skycraft.scene.ash_reading.0: Sit. Close your eyes. Breathe the smoke. The ancestors will tell me what you are, and you will not like all of it.
story.skycraft.scene.ash_reading.1: A stranger who walks between camps. Not one of us, and not one of them. The ancestors find that funny. So do I.
story.skycraft.scene.ash_vision.0: On the slopes of Red Mountain, the ash wind drops all at once. In the silence, figures of smoke rise around you: hunters, mothers, children, and old wise women with bright eyes.
story.skycraft.scene.ash_vision.1: The mountain dreams, and its dreams are poison. Keep the clans together, stranger. Apart, the ash will bury them one by one.
story.skycraft.scene.azura.0: Child of the twilight. A sorcerer has stolen my Star and twisted it into a prison for his own soul. Find him in the drowned fort of Ilinalta's Deep, and cleanse it.
story.skycraft.scene.barbas.0: Hey, friend. Yes, the dog is talking. Name's Barbas. My master, Clavicus Vile, and I had a little disagreement. Help me get back to him?
story.skycraft.scene.barbas.1: The dog trots ahead toward Haemar's Shame, tail wagging, as if it knows exactly where you're going.
story.skycraft.scene.bl_dragon_letter.0: Eruvan. Dragons over Skyrim, and now over the Jerall. Esbern says the old sky-watch signs are true. Watch your peaks.
story.skycraft.scene.bl_dragon_letter.1: And tell your new recruit that a dragon is not killed by courage alone. Take the head, take the wing, and do not stand in front of it.
story.skycraft.scene.bl_oath.0: Cloud Ruler Temple sits on its cliff above Bruma, snow on its curved Akaviri roofs. In the great hall, a single brazier burns before the dragon banner.
story.skycraft.scene.bl_oath.1: We don't have an Emperor to guard. We have a world full of dragons and a Dominion that wants us dead. That will have to do.
story.skycraft.scene.bl_oath.2: Swear to watch the sky and keep the old oath, and you are one of us. Few enough are left to hear it.
story.skycraft.scene.bl_pale_pass.0: At the heart of Pale Pass, frost ghosts gather around an armoured figure kneeling over a sword. It rises as you approach.
story.skycraft.scene.bl_pale_pass.1: We held this pass for a lord who never came. If you carry his oath, take the blade and earn it.
story.skycraft.scene.boethiah.0: My champion grows soft. Kill him, take his place, and I will dress you in my mail. Betrayal is the only true virtue.
story.skycraft.scene.burning.0: Down on the Solitude square, an effigy of King Olaf burns, and the whole city sings your restored verse.
story.skycraft.scene.burning.1: Listen to them! Two hundred years since anyone sang it right. You've saved the festival, and maybe the College.
story.skycraft.scene.call_odahviing.0: You call the name into the open sky above Whiterun. For a long moment, nothing.
story.skycraft.scene.clavicus.0: You brought back my dog. Wonderful. Now kill him with the axe, and I'll give you the Masque. Or give me back the axe and keep your sentimental attachments.
story.skycraft.scene.clavicus.1: Don't listen to him. I'm a good dog.
story.skycraft.scene.council.0: Jarl Ulfric. General Tullius. You are here because the Dragonborn asked it. Sit. Speak. Shout if you must, but not here.
story.skycraft.scene.council.1: The talk goes long into the night. In the end the generals sign: a truce until the dragon is dealt with.
story.skycraft.scene.cr_investiture.0: Torches ring the mouth of Anahbi's tomb. Crown lords in white and gold stand silent while an old singer chants the names of the dead, one after another, back to the drowning of Yokuda.
story.skycraft.scene.cr_investiture.1: My daughter kneels where I knelt, and where my father knelt before me. If any here deny her right, let them say so before the ancestors.
story.skycraft.scene.cr_investiture.2: From the dunes behind the gathering comes the scrape of drawn steel.
story.skycraft.scene.cr_lord_of_the_crow: In Yokuda, a sword-singer who saved a lord's line became part of that line. We have forgotten much since the crossing. Not that.
Anahbi carried this blade when the Ra Gada came ashore. It has waited long enough in the dark.
The lords touch their brows and then their hilts, the old salute, and speak your name as one of their own.
story.skycraft.scene.ct_boss.0: The Council Club falls quiet as you walk in. Sovor Trandel sets down his cup and stands.
story.skycraft.scene.ct_boss.1: Dalam Gavyn wanted to sell the Tong to the East Empire Company for a pension. You buried him instead. Dren says the Club is yours.
story.skycraft.scene.ct_boss.2: Boss of the Tong in Balmora. Keep the outlanders nervous and the coin flowing, and you'll do fine.
story.skycraft.scene.ct_dren.0: You know what the outlanders call us? Criminals. The Imperials take our ebony, our glass, our land, and call it law. We take it back, and it's crime.
story.skycraft.scene.ct_dren.1: I don't care about their words. I care that Dunmer coin stays in Dunmer hands. Do your work and you'll never go hungry.
story.skycraft.scene.cultists.0: You are no Dragonborn! The true Dragonborn is coming. Miraak will take what you stole.
story.skycraft.scene.dagon.0: The Razor is mine. Its pieces are scattered by thieves and scholars. Reforge it at my shrine, and offer me the fool who brought you there.
story.skycraft.scene.dbc_lucien_framed.0: I never wrote those orders. Someone in the Black Hand has been forging my seal and feeding our own people to the Family's knives.
story.skycraft.scene.dbc_lucien_framed.1: The Hand thinks I'm the traitor. They'll come for me before long. There is only one who knows the truth: the Night Mother. Her crypt lies beneath Bravil.
story.skycraft.scene.dbc_night_mother.0: In the crypt below Bravil, a stone coffin stands among cold candles. A woman's voice speaks from inside it, soft and very close.
story.skycraft.scene.dbc_night_mother.1: My Speaker is innocent. The one who betrayed my children wears their trust like a cloak, and you have just torn it from him.
story.skycraft.scene.dbc_night_mother.2: Hear me now, and only you. You will be my Listener. My words will come to you, and through you to the Family.
story.skycraft.scene.dbc_purification.0: The note is in Lucien's hand and bears the Black Hand's seal. Its instruction is short: the Cheydinhal Sanctuary harbours a traitor, and the Sanctuary must be cleansed.
story.skycraft.scene.dbc_purification.1: Below, the Family is at supper. Someone laughs at one of Vicente's stories. The order does not say which of them is the traitor.
The dragon's flesh burns away like paper. A storm of light pours out of the bones and into you.
By the Nine... it went into you. You're Dragonborn! The old stories said the Dragonborn could steal a dragon's power.
My grandmother told me about the Dragonborn. I never thought I'd see one.
story.skycraft.scene.dragonslayer.0: When you step back into Skyrim, every dragon in the land seems to be gathered on the Throat of the World, circling.
story.skycraft.scene.dragonslayer.1: The World-Eater is gone. Dovahkiin, you have done what none of us could. The dov will remember this.
story.skycraft.scene.dragonslayer.2: Dovahkiin. When you call, I will come. Alduin was never your equal.
story.skycraft.scene.duel.0: A shehai is the soul made into a blade. Draw yours, if you have one. Mine has been waiting a long time.
story.skycraft.scene.earth_stone.0: Your Voice slams into the stone. The black shell around it shatters, and the townsfolk who were building it blink, as if waking.
story.skycraft.scene.earth_stone.1: The stone is cleansed. Somewhere far off, someone screams in frustration.
story.skycraft.scene.eec_charter.0: A colony that pays, a factor who stole and was caught, a lost ship's accounts recovered from the Sea of Ghosts. That is more than most companies bring me.
story.skycraft.scene.eec_charter.1: The Company's charter is renewed for twenty years, with the Emperor's seal. Tell Ponius he owes you a great deal. I suspect he knows.
These are his letters. Company ebony sold to smugglers for half its worth, and the difference in his own pocket. For years.
You think Ebonheart cares? This colony survives because I make it profitable. Guards! Our guest is leaving. Permanently.
story.skycraft.scene.emperor.0: So. The Dark Brotherhood. I knew someone would come. Do me one favor: find the man who paid for this, and do to him what you are about to do to me.
story.skycraft.scene.emperor.1: The Emperor of Tamriel does not reach for a weapon.
story.skycraft.scene.eye_anomaly.0: A shock wave rolls out of the Hall of the Elements. The Eye of Magnus burns bright, and Ancano stands before it, laughing.
story.skycraft.scene.eye_anomaly.1: None of you understand what this is. I do. Stay back, or be unmade.
story.skycraft.scene.eye_anomaly.2: Wild magic spills into the courtyard and takes shape: anomalies, crackling and hungry.
story.skycraft.scene.eye_found.0: Look at it. A great orb of pure magic, sleeping under a Nord tomb. We must take it to the College, carefully. Very carefully.
story.skycraft.scene.eye_sealed.0: It is done. The Eye is too dangerous for this world, and the Order will keep it where no one can reach it. You have done well, Arch-Mage.
story.skycraft.scene.eye_sealed.1: Arch-Mage! Ha! I always said you had a head for the Arcane.
story.skycraft.scene.falion_ritual.0: At the summoning circle the marsh mist turns gold with the first light. Falion raises the black soul gem, and it drinks.
story.skycraft.scene.falion_ritual.1: Hold still. The thing in your blood is leaving, and it does not go quietly.
story.skycraft.scene.falion_ritual.2: Cold rushes through you, then warmth: the sun on your face, and nothing in it but light.
story.skycraft.scene.fb_council.0: When our grandfathers came ashore, the Crowns kept the swords and the Forebears kept the harbours. Hammerfell has needed both ever since, whatever the lords in Sentinel say.
story.skycraft.scene.fb_council.1: Half the captains in this port owe their ships to you tonight. Sailors remember a debt longer than lords do.
story.skycraft.scene.fb_council.2: So does the council. By its vote you sit with us now, a Lord of the Forebears. Try not to look so surprised. It encourages people to haggle with you.
story.skycraft.scene.fb_harbor_night.0: Lamps burn low along Taneth's harbour. Somewhere among the warehouses oil has been poured; you can smell it over the salt.
story.skycraft.scene.fb_harbor_night.1: My crew is on the quay with buckets and boathooks. Find the man with the torch before he finds a spark.
In the cellar of the Blackwood hall, a sickly young tree grows from a trough of black-marsh mud, its bark scored with tapping cuts.
You think we are thieves of contracts. We are the future of your trade. Steel that does not tire, does not fear, does not ask questions.
Steel that goes mad and kills the client. No. The Guild ends this tonight.
story.skycraft.scene.fg_master.0: I've led this Guild through lean years and worse ones. My son is alive because of you, and the Guild still has a name because of you.
story.skycraft.scene.fg_master.1: I am tired, and I am done. The hall needs a Master who can still swing a blade. Modryn agrees. So do I.
story.skycraft.scene.fg_master.2: Vilena unbuckles the Guildmaster's sword and lays it across your hands. Around the hall, the members raise their cups.
story.skycraft.scene.fg_sap_revealed.0: This is no tonic. It is the sap of a Hist, the trees that remember my people before they had names.
story.skycraft.scene.fg_sap_revealed.1: Among the Saxhleel it is taken in rite and in reverence. Drunk by the cup by dry-skins, it would make them strong, and fearless, and then mad.
story.skycraft.scene.fg_sap_revealed.2: That explains the Blackwood men who keep fighting with a sword through the lung. The Company is brewing its own soldiers.
story.skycraft.scene.fs_briarheart.0: In the heart of Druadach Redoubt, Kaie draws a briar-root through the bear's heart and holds it over the fire until it smokes. The Forsworn beat their shields.
story.skycraft.scene.fs_briarheart.1: Brave heart, old heart, give your courage to the root. Root, take the warrior who brought it, and never let them run.
story.skycraft.scene.fs_briarheart.2: From tonight you carry the briar. The Reach is yours to guard, Briarheart. Do not make me regret trusting a stranger twice.
story.skycraft.scene.fs_framed.0: Eltrys lies at the foot of the old shrine with a guardsman's knife between his ribs. Three guards step out of the shadows behind you.
story.skycraft.scene.fs_framed.1: Found standing over the body, weren't you? Thonar Silver-Blood said you'd come. You're going to Cidhna Mine, and you're going to stay there.
story.skycraft.scene.fs_king_in_rags.0: For twenty years the Silver-Bloods have paid me to sit in this hole and give my orders from it. They think they own the King in Rags. They own a cage.
story.skycraft.scene.fs_king_in_rags.1: Every death in Markarth's streets was mine, and every one of them was paid for in Silver-Blood coin. Now I am done waiting. Are you coming with me?
story.skycraft.scene.gb_master_of_the_vo: The four Masters stand at the corners of the courtyard. They speak your name together, very softly, and the mountain answers. Snow lifts from every roof of High Hrothgar at once.
Many come to us for power. Very few learn that the strongest Voice is the one that chooses silence. You chose it when it was hard.
Go with the Masters' blessing, and walk the Way of the Voice. Whatever the world calls you, here you are called friend, and Master.
story.skycraft.scene.gb_quiet_word.0: The courtyard is silent but for the wind. Master Einarth sits across from you, eyes closed, and does not move for an hour.
story.skycraft.scene.gb_quiet_word.1: A Word is not a weapon you pick up. It is a truth about the world. FUS is Force, yes. But force is only the shape that patience takes when it runs out.
story.skycraft.scene.gb_quiet_word.2: Jurgen Windcaller learned that at Red Mountain, where his Voice failed him before the Dunmer. He spent the rest of his life listening instead of shouting. So shall we.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_bond_renewed.0: The Silvenar takes the Green Lady's hands. For a moment the leaves overhead stop moving, though the wind has not.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_bond_renewed.1: When she bleeds, I feel it. When she is far away, the people grow restless and do not know why. We are bound, the two of us, and through us, everyone.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_bond_renewed.2: And when he worries, I cannot hunt. Thank you for bringing me home before he worried himself into a fever.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_spinners_tale.0: Long ago, a hunter grew tired of meat and cut a branch to roast roots on. Only one branch. The tree did not forget.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_spinners_tale.1: The grove around it grew sour and sharp, and the spriggans came to tend its anger. Every Bosmer child hears this tale. Most think it is a story.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_spinners_tale.2: You have seen the grove. You know better. The Pact is not a law we keep. It is a promise the forest keeps back, as long as we keep ours.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_voice.0: The forest has spoken to me about you. Not in words. In a feeling of being listened to, which is rarer than you would think.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_voice.1: When I cannot travel, my voice must. I name you its keeper. Carry it carefully. It is everyone's.
story.skycraft.scene.gp_voice.2: The Green Lady sets a bow of polished bone and horn across your hands. No living wood went into it.
story.skycraft.scene.green_heart.0: Who walks in my wood without the Pact? Ah. You come with the Spinner's word. Take the seed, then, and plant it where the forest bled.
story.skycraft.scene.greybeards_ro.0: You have the Voice, untrained but strong. Hear now the second word of Force: RO, Balance. Let it steady the first.
story.skycraft.scene.greybeards_ro.1: And one more, for the trial of the gate: WULD, Whirlwind. Run where no feet could carry you.
The word rolls down from the Throat of the World like thunder. Every soul in Whiterun hears it.
story.skycraft.scene.harbinger.0: There. Sovngarde, at last. You lead the Circle now, Harbinger. Lead it well.
story.skycraft.scene.harbinger.1: Kodlak's spirit fades into the cold light of the tomb. The Companions bow their heads.
story.skycraft.scene.harkon_falls.0: No... the prophecy was mine... the sun would be mine...
story.skycraft.scene.harkon_falls.1: It's over. He was my father, and I'm glad it's over. Let's go home. Wherever that is now.
story.skycraft.scene.harkon_gift.0: You returned my daughter. I am in your debt, and I pay my debts. I offer you my blood, the gift of the Vampire Lord.
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_cart.0: A cart rattles over frozen ruts. Your wrists are bound; the man beside you wears the blue of a rebel.
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_cart.1: Awake at last. You walked into an Imperial ambush meant for us. Bad luck, friend.
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_cart.2: Prisoners off the cart! Step up to the block when your name is called.
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_cart.4: Before the axe can fall, a roar splits the sky. Something vast and black lands on the watchtower.
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_cart.5: Dragon! Everyone, to the keep! You, prisoner, with me or with him, but MOVE!
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_escape.0: Daylight. Behind you, smoke climbs from what was Helgen. Far off, the black dragon wheels north over the mountains.
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_escape.1: Riverwood is just down the road. My sister Gerdur will help us, if you sided with me back there.
story.skycraft.scene.helgen_escape.2: My uncle Alvor is the smith in Riverwood. He'll put us up. And someone has to warn Whiterun.
story.skycraft.scene.hermaeus.0: Knowledge is the only treasure that grows when shared, and the only treasure I keep for myself. Read, mortal. Read, and become more than you were.
story.skycraft.scene.hircine.0: Sinding stole my ring and cursed himself with it. A fine hunt: the hunted beast who wears my favor. Find him in Bloated Man's Grotto, and choose your prey.
story.skycraft.scene.hist.0: We remember the root before the root. We remember you, warm-blood, though you have never come here before.
story.skycraft.scene.hist.1: The Hist speaks to you? Then you are touched. The blight is lifting.
story.skycraft.scene.hl_curio_grant.0: Nileno tells me you've saved half of Balmora from the Tong. How heroic. How useful. A House needs strongholds, and you need a roof.
story.skycraft.scene.hl_curio_grant.1: There's a lovely bit of rock on the Odai plateau. Build something there. Something sturdy, and preferably with a nice bathhouse.
story.skycraft.scene.hl_grandmaster.0: In the Hlaalu Council chamber in Vivec, the councilors argue over coin, then over each other, then, finally, over you.
story.skycraft.scene.hl_grandmaster.1: Rethan Manor stands. The Tong is beaten in Balmora. The ebony flows and the ledgers balance. I can think of no one better.
story.skycraft.scene.hl_grandmaster.2: Nor I, and I can think of a great many people. Grandmaster of House Hlaalu, then. Try to look surprised.
story.skycraft.scene.ic_blessing.0: In the great dome of the Temple of the One, the Primate stands beneath the windows of the Nine. Colored light falls across the floor like water.
story.skycraft.scene.ic_blessing.1: You fed the poor, quieted the dead, walked the roads of the Divines, scoured a Daedric shrine and nursed a sick city back to health.
story.skycraft.scene.ic_blessing.2: The Nine do not need us to be perfect. They need us to keep showing up. You have. Kneel, and receive their blessing.
story.skycraft.scene.ic_catacombs.0: The catacomb air is cold and still. Then the candles gutter all at once, and somewhere in the dark, bone scrapes on stone.
story.skycraft.scene.ic_catacombs.1: Arkay keeps the door between life and death. When the dead walk, someone has propped it open. Close it, gently if you can.
story.skycraft.scene.karliah_truth.0: I didn't murder Gallus. Mercer Frey did, and he stole the Skeleton Key from the Twilight Sepulcher. The Guild's bad luck is Nocturnal's displeasure.
story.skycraft.scene.karliah_truth.1: Gallus kept a journal. It's in an old script I can't read. If we can read it, the Guild will believe us.
story.skycraft.scene.kd_banner_found.0: The banner hangs above a stone bier in the deepest vault of Cath Bedraud, untouched by damp or moth. Beneath it lies a knight in red-lacquered mail, hands folded on a sword.
story.skycraft.scene.kd_banner_found.1: Sir Aubert, who carried it at the order's founding. They told us he fell defending a crossing. They never said where they laid him.
story.skycraft.scene.kd_knighthood.0: The hall falls quiet. The Banner of the Red Wyrm hangs above the dais for the first time in two centuries.
story.skycraft.scene.kd_knighthood.1: You kept vigil, you carried a lady safe through Glenumbra, you killed a dragon and took the lists from Camlorn's best. And you brought our founding home.
story.skycraft.scene.kd_knighthood.2: Kneel. Rise a knight of the Dragon, and a captain of this order. Daggerfall's gate is yours to keep.
story.skycraft.scene.kn9_crusader.0: The avatar of Umaril breaks apart in a storm of light. For a long moment the ruin is silent. Then, somewhere far above, bells ring.
story.skycraft.scene.kn9_crusader.1: It is finished. The Nine see you, Divine Crusader. Keep the order, and keep the faith, when no one else does.
story.skycraft.scene.kn9_umaril_falls.0: You strike down my flesh, little knight. Flesh I can spare. Meridia's realm keeps my spirit. I will walk out of it again.
story.skycraft.scene.kn9_umaril_falls.1: Umaril's body crumbles into golden ash, but a light flees upward from it, into the dark of the ruin, and is gone.
story.skycraft.scene.kn9_vision.0: The shrine is cold until you kneel. Then the air fills with the sound of a great battle, very far away and very long ago.
story.skycraft.scene.kn9_vision.1: I was the Divines' hound, and I hunted the Ayleid kings until the last of them knelt. One I could not finish. Umaril. He is coming back.
story.skycraft.scene.kn9_vision.2: My helm and gauntlets lie with my knights near Anvil. My mace lies where the elves hid it. Take them up. Finish what I began.
story.skycraft.scene.kodlak_spirit.0: My Shield-Siblings. You have freed me from the hunt. The Wolf Spirit still holds the others; you know what must be done.
story.skycraft.scene.kodlak_spirit.1: Fight it here, in Ysgramor's hall, and I will pass to Sovngarde with my head held high.
story.skycraft.scene.kr_roses_oath.0: In the chapel of the Rose, every knight in Wayrest stands with a white rose pinned over the heart. The candles have burned low.
story.skycraft.scene.kr_roses_oath.1: We swear to keep faith with the weak, to speak truth to the mighty and to suffer no cruelty in our sight. You have kept that oath before you ever spoke it.
story.skycraft.scene.kr_roses_oath.2: Say the words, and take the rose. The order is yours to lead in the field, as Lord of the Rose.
story.skycraft.scene.kr_the_yield.0: Sir Garrick lies in the sand of the duelling ground with his helm knocked askew. The crowd is silent. In the gallery, the Chancellor's chair is empty.
story.skycraft.scene.kr_the_yield.1: The trial is decided. Before Stendarr and the court of Wayrest, the Chancellor's cause has failed. Guards, find him.
story.skycraft.scene.kvatch_gate.0: The gate stands in the hills above Kvatch: twin spikes of black stone around a membrane of fire. It hums. It breathes.
story.skycraft.scene.kvatch_gate.1: Mortal! The Prince's gate opens again. Step through, and burn with the rest.
story.skycraft.scene.labyrinthian.0: Sahrot qostiid! Who wakes Morokei in his own halls? Your magicka will feed my staff.
story.skycraft.scene.lgc_fort_sutch.0: Fort Sutch smells of ash and hot iron. Where a gate to Oblivion once burned, a scar of red rock still pulses in the ground, and the Daedra have come back to it.
story.skycraft.scene.lgc_fort_sutch.1: Hold the walls. Whatever comes out of that scar, it doesn't reach the Gold Coast road.
story.skycraft.scene.lgc_kvatch_walls.0: Stone, mortar, and a mason who knows what she's doing. Kvatch hasn't seen a convoy that reached it whole in a long time.
story.skycraft.scene.lgc_kvatch_walls.1: Give me a season and your walls will stand when the hills burn again. Which, from the look of them, they might.
story.skycraft.scene.lgc_kvatch_walls.2: Behind the ruined chapel, the first new stones are set while the soldiers watch the ridge.
story.skycraft.scene.malacath.0: Largashbur forgot me. Their chief grew fat and lazy. Bring me the troll's fat, kill the giant who mocks them, and I will remember Largashbur again.
story.skycraft.scene.malyn.0: You've come for the Star? I am the Star now. Come in, if you like being destroyed.
story.skycraft.scene.mephala.0: Little ears, little whispers. The Jarl's son hears me, and so do you. My blade sleeps in this palace. Wake it with a lie.
story.skycraft.scene.meridia.0: My temple is defiled by a necromancer who raises my honored dead as puppets. Purge Kilkreath, and Dawnbreaker will be yours.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_archmage.0: Mannimarco is dust. Do you understand what that means? Generations of mages will never know his name, because of you.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_archmage.1: I am old, and this fight has taken more of me than I like to admit. The Council agrees: the University needs younger hands.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_archmage.2: Arch-Mage. I suppose I'll have to stop correcting your spelling.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_king_of_worms.0: Traven sends a student? I was ancient when his tower was a field of mud. Every soul in this cave is mine. So is yours, now.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_king_of_worms.1: Kneel, and you may serve as you rot. Stand, and you will serve all the same.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_necromancers_moo: Under the moon, the necromancers' altar shudders. A ray of grey light falls on the soul gem in its cradle, and the gem drinks it until it is black.
Somewhere far off, in a voice like dry leaves, someone laughs.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_worm_council.0: When I banned necromancy in the Guild, I knew some would leave. I did not expect them to come back hunting us.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_worm_council.1: These are not hedge-wizards. They answer to the King of Worms. Mannimarco.
story.skycraft.scene.mg_worm_council.2: Then we know who we are fighting. Find out what they are preparing. I want to see it before it sees us.
story.skycraft.scene.miraak_appears.0: You've come far, but not far enough. Every soul you take, I will take from you. Solstheim is mine already. Soon, so is Skyrim.
story.skycraft.scene.miraak_appears.1: A masked figure in robes of tentacle and scale lifts his hand, and the dragon you just slew goes still. Its soul streams into him instead of you.
story.skycraft.scene.miraak_falls.0: Miraak, you thought you could hide your plans from me? You were mine from the moment you opened my book. And now, so is your successor.
story.skycraft.scene.miraak_falls.1: Tentacles pierce Miraak through. His power, and the souls he stole, pour out of him and into you.
story.skycraft.scene.molag.0: The priest came to cleanse my house. How charming. Bring him to me, and I'll give you something heavy.
story.skycraft.scene.molag_coldharbour.0: You did well. Now see what you serve. Walk my city, and remember it when you sleep.
story.skycraft.scene.molag_coldharbour.1: Chains lash out of the floor. The house folds away, and a black sky opens over burning ruins.
story.skycraft.scene.moons.0: Both moons rise over the Temple of the Two Moons, and the silver lattice on the altar catches their light and throws it across the stones.
story.skycraft.scene.moons.1: Jone and Jode dance again. The Lunar Lattice holds. The Mane will want to hear this.
story.skycraft.scene.mp_dark_moon.0: The censer flares, and for a breath both moons seem to hang low over the ruin, one silver, one pale red.
story.skycraft.scene.mp_dark_moon.1: Do you see? The Dro-m'Athra are Khajiit who walked off the Lattice and into the dark between the moons. Namiira's children. They are not evil, exactly. They are lost, and they are hungry.
story.skycraft.scene.mp_dark_moon.2: We do not hate them. We send them home. Sometimes home is very far away.
Masser rises, then Secunda. Azadhi and a temple moon-singer turn slow circles on the steps, one following Jone, one following Jode, never touching, never apart.
This is the Dance. Every Khajiit dances it, from the crib to the pyre. Some dance it well. Most dance it badly. A few forget the steps.
Dance with us, walker. Badly is fine. The moons are patient.
story.skycraft.scene.mp_voice.0: The Mane has heard of a walker who carries pilgrims, feeds the fields, and sends the lost children of the dark moon home.
story.skycraft.scene.mp_voice.1: The Mane has many voices. Priests, bishops, clan mothers. One more will not crowd the room. Kneel.
story.skycraft.scene.mp_voice.2: The Mane lays a braided cord of silver and red across your shoulders. In the temple, the moon-singers begin a low and very old song.
story.skycraft.scene.mt_code.0: Hear the code. We kill only by writ. We kill only the one named. We leave our writ on the body, so all know it was lawful.
story.skycraft.scene.mt_code.1: Kill without a writ, and you are a murderer like any other, and the Tong will issue a writ for you. Do you understand?
story.skycraft.scene.mt_exalted.0: The Brotherhood's cell in Vvardenfell is gone. Their killers broke our law and mocked our goddess, and you answered both.
story.skycraft.scene.mt_exalted.1: The Tong has few Exalted Masters. You are one now. Wear the title as you wear the writ: openly, and without apology.
story.skycraft.scene.mt_webspinner.0: Eno Hlaalu lays the three threads on the floor of his chamber. They move, slowly, weaving themselves into a pattern no hand made.
story.skycraft.scene.mt_webspinner.1: My children keep their law, and my threads come home. Good. The Night Mother's brood is nesting in my house. Cut them out.
story.skycraft.scene.namira.0: Eola keeps my old feast. Join it. Taste what others fear, and you will never hunger as they do.
story.skycraft.scene.night_mother.0: My child. You have been chosen. Go to the Emperor's man in Volunruud, and listen.
story.skycraft.scene.night_mother.1: She spoke! She spoke to you! Oh, the Listener, the Listener has come!
story.skycraft.scene.nightingale_oath.0: In the hall of the Nightingales, Karliah leads you before a great stone circle. The shadows deepen until they feel like a held breath.
story.skycraft.scene.nightingale_oath.1: So. Another stands before me. Serve me as Nightingale, in life and after, and I will grant you my shadow. Return what was stolen.
story.skycraft.scene.nightingale_oath.2: That was Nocturnal. Now we hunt Mercer.
story.skycraft.scene.nocturnal_return.0: The Skeleton Key slides into the Ebonmere. The pool of darkness ripples, and a figure of shadow and feathers rises from it.
story.skycraft.scene.nocturnal_return.1: The Key is home. You have done what you swore. The Guild's luck is restored, and you are mine, Nightingale. Walk in shadow.
story.skycraft.scene.nocturnal_return.2: Karliah. I'm free. Thank you, friend.
story.skycraft.scene.oblivion_return.0: You tear the Sigil Stone from its flame. The tower screams, the red sky folds in on itself, and the Deadlands spit you back into Cyrodiil's clean air. Behind you the gate's fire gutters out.
story.skycraft.scene.odahviing_deal.0: Hah! The great yoke. You are clever, for a joor. Alduin's eyrie is Skuldafn, far east, beyond the reach of your feet.
story.skycraft.scene.odahviing_deal.1: Free me and I will carry you there. Alduin has shown himself weak. Perhaps it is time the dov chose a stronger master.
story.skycraft.scene.odahviing_flight.0: Hold fast. I will not fly gently. Skuldafn waits in the mountains where the snow never melts.
story.skycraft.scene.odahviing_flight.1: The ground falls away. Skyrim spreads beneath you like a map, white and green and grey, and then the eastern peaks rush up.
story.skycraft.scene.odahviing_name.0: The name you need is Odahviing: Snow, Hunter, Wing. He is Alduin's lieutenant, and proud. Call him, and he will come.
story.skycraft.scene.olaf_rises.0: Free me, and I'll sing the truth of Olaf One-Eye one last time. He stole my verse and buried me in the dark for it.
story.skycraft.scene.olaf_rises.1: You'll not have it! I am King! I am the hero of the songs!
story.skycraft.scene.orc_honored_chief.0: The Hall of the Clans is full: chiefs, wise-women and smiths from every stronghold in Wrothgar, standing shoulder to shoulder under the smoke-black rafters.
story.skycraft.scene.orc_honored_chief.1: Outsider, Blood-Kin, smith's runner, ogre-killer, and today the one who put Bazrag on his back in front of all of you. The Code is plain. Strength is honoured.
story.skycraft.scene.orc_honored_chief.2: From this day you are an Honored Chief of the Orsimer. You have no stronghold of your own, so you will be welcome in all of them. Try not to eat them out of house and home.
story.skycraft.scene.orc_the_code.0: You went to the Furious One's shrine and came back. That is the first part of any answer. Now hear the rest.
story.skycraft.scene.orc_the_code.1: The stronghold is stronger than any Orc in it. The chief leads until someone stronger takes his place. What words cannot settle, blood-price settles. And we kneel to no one, not to kings and not to gods. Malacath least of all; he would spit on it.
story.skycraft.scene.orc_the_code.2: Murbul presses ash from her fire against your brow with her thumb. It is still warm.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_after.0: He fled to Sovngarde, to feed on the souls of the honored dead. Only the dovah know the way there.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_after.1: Trap one of his own. Make it carry you. A dragon called with its own name cannot refuse to come.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_meet.0: Wings beat out of the cloud. An ancient grey dragon lands on the word wall at the summit and lowers its head.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_meet.1: Drem yol lok. Greetings, wunduniik, traveler. Before we speak, let us speak in the old way. Show me your Thu'um.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_meet.2: Here is a word for you: YOL. Fire. Speak it to me.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_slain.0: So be it. Perhaps it was always meant to end this way. Remember what I taught you, Dovahkiin.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_yol.0: Yes. You have the gift of our kind. Now hear me. Dragonrend cannot be taught: it was born of the hatred of mortals.
story.skycraft.scene.paarthurnax_yol.1: Long ago an Elder Scroll was used here, at this place, and time was wounded. Bring a Scroll back to the wound and you will see the heroes who first spoke it.
story.skycraft.scene.peryite.0: The Taskmaster has a task. My afflicted wander from Bthardamz, led by a fallen elf named Orchendor. Order requires that he be ended.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_breach_sealed.0: Feel that? The world just exhaled. A breach is a wound where a moment that should never happen pushes into one that did.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_breach_sealed.1: The Daedra smell them, the way sharks smell blood. Someone is opening them on purpose. That is worse than any Daedra.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_ritemaster.0: Iachesis lifts the Horologe. Its rings spin until they blur, then stop, all at once, aligned. The torn air over Artaeum closes like an eye.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_ritemaster.1: There. The isle is ours again. And the rite needed two pairs of hands, which I did not tell you, because you would have been nervous.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_ritemaster.2: The Council has agreed. Few outsiders learn the Old Ways this quickly. Fewer still live long enough to teach them. Be the second kind.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_vision.0: The fog closes in. For a moment there is no ground under you, only grey, and the slow toll of a bell somewhere very far away.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_vision.1: We have watched you for longer than you have been watching yourself. Come west, to the isle that is not always there.
story.skycraft.scene.ps_vision.2: When the fog lifts, you are standing on a pale shore you have never seen, and an elf in a hooded robe is waiting as though you had an appointment.
story.skycraft.scene.rd_archmaster.0: The Council Hall of Ald'ruhn falls silent. Bolvyn Venim kneels in the dust of the duelling floor, his blade beside him.
story.skycraft.scene.rd_archmaster.1: By the old law, the challenge is answered. House Redoran has a new Archmaster.
story.skycraft.scene.rd_archmaster.2: Duty, honor, endurance. You have shown all three. Lead us well.
story.skycraft.scene.rd_varvur_freed.0: My son is free. And the coin that framed him came from a hand signing itself 'V'. We both know whose hand that is.
story.skycraft.scene.rd_varvur_freed.1: Venim has led this House toward pride and petty vengeance for too long. When the Council meets, I will name you as his challenger.
story.skycraft.scene.red_mountain.0: The heart beats still, outlander. The Tribunal is gone; the House of Troubles stirs. Sleep, and wake as one of us.
story.skycraft.scene.red_mountain.1: Ash rises from every vent of the mountain. Shapes stand up out of it.
story.skycraft.scene.rk_freed.0: Three months in that pen. They said this one was a rebel. This one was a farmer. Now, perhaps, he will be a rebel after all.
story.skycraft.scene.rk_freed.1: Everyone says that, the first night. Eat, sleep. If you still mean it in the morning, we will find you a blade.
story.skycraft.scene.rk_laughing_blade.0: The camp is loud tonight. Somebody is playing a drum badly, and nobody minds.
story.skycraft.scene.rk_laughing_blade.1: Ri'Vasha sold our grain to the Thalmor and our sons to the Thalmor's prisons. Tonight he sells nothing.
story.skycraft.scene.rk_laughing_blade.2: The Mane's priests will call us bandits. The nobles will call us beasts. Let them. Tonight, you are a Laughing Blade, and we laugh last.
story.skycraft.scene.saarthal_vision.0: When you lift the amulet, the chamber goes silent and a robed figure stands where there was no one a moment ago.
story.skycraft.scene.saarthal_vision.1: Listen well. What lies within Saarthal is dangerous beyond your understanding. The Psijic Order will be watching. Act wisely.
story.skycraft.scene.saarthal_vision.2: Then he is simply gone, and a sealed wall cracks open behind you.
story.skycraft.scene.sahloknir_rises.0: A black shape blots out the sun and settles on the burial mound. It speaks to the earth in its own tongue.
story.skycraft.scene.sahloknir_rises.2: The mound breaks apart. Bones knit and scales grow over them. A second dragon rises, and the black one turns to you.
story.skycraft.scene.sahloknir_rises.3: You do not even know what you are, little mortal. Sahloknir, kill it.
story.skycraft.scene.sanctuary_burns.0: Smoke rises from the Sanctuary's door. The Penitus Oculatus found it. The Black Door hangs broken.
story.skycraft.scene.sanctuary_burns.1: They came at dawn. Astrid sold us to them, and then they killed her too. We go to the old Sanctuary in Dawnstar. We finish this.
story.skycraft.scene.sanguine.0: You remember a drinking contest. You remember a lot of mead. Then you remember nothing at all, until you wake in a temple with a headache like a dragon's footstep.
story.skycraft.scene.sanguine.1: Ha! There you are. You were magnificent. Here, a souvenir of the best night anyone's had in a century.
story.skycraft.scene.serana_wakes.0: The stone sarcophagus in the heart of the crypt slides open. A pale woman steps out, blinking, an Elder Scroll strapped to her back.
story.skycraft.scene.serana_wakes.1: Who are you? How long was I in there? Never mind. I need to get home. Castle Volkihar, in the north sea. Will you take me?
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_end.0: In the deepest chamber of Driftshade Refuge, silver-tipped arrows lie in bundles beside tanning racks no one wants to look at too closely.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_end.1: It's done. Without Krev and without Varek, the rest will scatter like crows. Stendarr keep me from feeling glad of it. I feel glad of it anyway.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_end.2: Jorrvaskr will drink to you tonight, Vigilant or no. Don't tell Vilkas I said so.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_list.0: Look at these names. A tanner. A woodcutter. A farmer whose only crime was selling mutton to Jorrvaskr's kitchen.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_list.1: The Silver Hand say they hunt beasts. I have hunted beasts for twenty years. Beasts do not keep lists.
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath.0: Ah, a visitor! In the mind of Pelagius, of all places. He was so very interesting, before the strangling. Fix his little troubles and I'll go home. And you'll get a present!
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath.1: Leave me alone! Not you too! The Night Terrors, the Confidence, the Anger! They're all in here with me!
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath_isles.0: Splendid! You've earned a holiday. Come along, come along, mind the door. It bites. Only on Tuesdays.
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath_isles.1: A door that was not there a moment ago swings open on a sky of impossible colours.
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath_palace.0: My Isles! My city! My cheese! Take the staff, little mortal, and spread a little madness. Now off you pop, I have a lunch to forget.
story.skycraft.scene.skjor_dead.0: Skjor went after the Silver Hand alone while we slept. They left him in the road like a hide on a rack.
story.skycraft.scene.skjor_dead.1: Gallows Rock. That's where they keep their trophies. We take it apart, all of it.
story.skycraft.scene.solitude_falls.0: Castle Dour's gate falls in. General Tullius stands alone in his war room, sword drawn, his officers dead around him.
story.skycraft.scene.solitude_falls.1: It's done. Skyrim is ours. Sovngarde will sing of this day.
