story.skycraft.scene.soul_cairn.0: A portal of red light opens in the courtyard. Beyond it, purple skies and drifting souls: the Soul Cairn, a realm of Oblivion.
story.skycraft.scene.soul_cairn.1: Serana? You came. Then Harkon is still chasing that prophecy. I hid the other Scroll here so he could never have it. Take it, and stop him.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_heroes.0: I am Tsun, shield-thane of Shor. None enter the Hall of Valor without facing me, but you, you have come for other business.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_heroes.1: We have waited a long age to finish what we began on the mountain. Lead us, Dragonborn.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_heroes.2: The mist thins. Alduin circles the Hall, devouring the lost. Clear the sky with your Voice and bring him down.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_portal.0: The staff slots into the pedestal. A column of light swallows the sky, and the stones of Skuldafn fall away beneath you.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_hist_dream.0: The sap is bitter, then sweet, then gone. The marsh tilts. The trees lean down and look at you with no eyes at all.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_hist_dream.1: Shadow-born. You were laid in the dark and hatched in the dark. The dark is not your enemy. It is your egg. Hunt now.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_speaker.0: The Tong came for us, and the Tong is buried in our mud. Hear me, all of you. The one who did this was born under the Shadow, like you, and is now more than you.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_speaker.1: I am old. I will need someone to speak for the Shadow when the King calls. Not yet. But soon.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_speaker.2: Around the enclave, the Shadowscales lower their heads and touch the ground. One by one, they hiss your name.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_the_traitor_name: Weighs-the-Coin. He was hatched two nests from mine. I taught him to hold a blade.
The Morag Tong pays well for the names of rivals. He gave them every one of us. Go after him, and do not let him reach the river.
story.skycraft.scene.stone_cleansed.0: Another stone of the All-Maker is clean. The wind on Solstheim smells a little more like the sea and a little less like ink.
story.skycraft.scene.summit.0: Hermaeus Mora gave me knowledge, and then chains. I will have neither. You came to my summit: then die here, little rival.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_gray_fox.0: The room in the Waterfront hideout is dark except for one lamp. A figure in a grey hood sits behind it, and his face slides out of memory as soon as you see it.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_gray_fox.1: Armand speaks well of you. I need someone who can go where I can't, and do it without leaving bodies for the Watch to count.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_gray_fox.2: This cowl was stolen from Nocturnal herself, long ago. It hides who I am from the whole world. Including the people I love. I mean to be rid of it.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_homecoming.0: This ring. I would know it anywhere. Where did you... no. He's home. He's in the courtyard, isn't he? I can feel it.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_homecoming.1: Millona Umbranox crosses the hall without another word. Through the window, two figures meet beside the fountain and do not let go.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_scroll_read.0: The Gray Fox unrolls the Elder Scroll. Light that is not quite light pours over his hands, and for a moment the hideout seems to remember a different past.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_scroll_read.1: There. It's done. The world will remember a man named Corvus Umbranox, Count of Anvil. He didn't vanish. He only went away for a while.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_scroll_read.2: And the cowl stays with the Guild. Someone has to wear it. I think it should be you.
story.skycraft.scene.th_high_justiciar.0: Orvanwe's family has served the Dominion for nine generations. He sold all nine of them for Windhelm gold.
story.skycraft.scene.th_high_justiciar.1: You found him, you judged him, and you did not hesitate. The Emissary has written to Alinor about you. I have been asked to read her letter aloud.
story.skycraft.scene.th_high_justiciar.2: The letter is short. It names you High Justiciar, and asks that you be given whatever you need.
story.skycraft.scene.th_reception.0: Music drifts through the embassy hall. Jarls' cousins and merchant princes hold their cups very carefully and smile at the Thalmor guards.
story.skycraft.scene.th_reception.1: Look at them. Every one of them hates us, and every one of them came. That is what power is: an invitation no one can afford to refuse.
story.skycraft.scene.th_reception.2: Mingle. Someone in this room has been selling my letters. Find out who before the wine runs out.
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.0: The Scroll unrolls itself. The world goes grey; the snow freezes in the air. You stand among three warriors of an age long past, watching Alduin fall from the sky.
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.1: Dragonrend has struck him! Now, while he is grounded!
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.3: It isn't enough. He won't die. Felldir, the Scroll! Use it now!
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.4: The vision tears apart. The three words of Dragonrend ring in your skull: JOOR, ZAH, FRUL. And above the summit, a black dragon descends.
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.5: Dovahkiin. You are too late. Your Shout is a toy in my claws.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_ilunibi.0: Deep in Ilunibi, the walls are crusted with ash and something like wet bark. Low chanting echoes from a chamber below.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_ilunibi.1: A pilgrim of the false gods. How sweet. Come closer. Dream with us. The Sleeper is waking, and he remembers you.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_patriarch.0: Beneath the High Fane, the Archcanon lays a hand on your brow. The light through the great windows is the color of Vivec's own city at dusk.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_patriarch.1: You walked the Graces, purged the Sixth House, healed the blighted, weighed justice and mercy, and stood fast at Ghostgate.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_patriarch.2: The Temple has many servants. It has few shepherds. Rise, Patriarch.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_archmagister.0: Gothren falls among his own enchanted pillars. The tower of Tel Aruhn shudders once, and is still.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_archmagister.1: By Telvanni law, the strong rule. Gothren refused to step aside. Now he has, permanently. Archmagister, the Council awaits you, mostly with resentment.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_council.0: The Telvanni Council House is a forest of grown stone and silence. The masters sit far apart, each pretending the others are not there.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_council.1: My new Mouth will speak for me today. Listen, or don't. You usually don't.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_council.2: At least this one has some manners. More than the last.
story.skycraft.scene.und_drinking_contes: Glirion slams two tankards on the table. The ale inside is dark, thick, and smells faintly of pine tar.
The rules are simple. We drink. Whoever's still upright at the end gets to talk. Whoever isn't gets carried.
Five tankards later, the hall is spinning and Glirion is singing a song about a troll and a bishop that has at least nine verses too many.
story.skycraft.scene.und_legend.0: The three of them stand around the old horn as if it were a sleeping animal. Then Glirion hangs it on the trophy wall, in the empty space that has waited there for years.
story.skycraft.scene.und_legend.1: Every Undaunted who ever lived has looked at that empty peg and lied about filling it. You didn't lie.
story.skycraft.scene.und_legend.2: Don't let it go to your head. Your name goes on the wall. The next idiot has to beat it.
story.skycraft.scene.und_pledges_counted: Barrow, ruin, tomb, pyramid, Dwemer pit. Five pledges, five cultures, and you came back with all your fingers.
Most of them come back with fewer. Glirion lost a toe in Volenfell and still won't tell anyone how.
It was a gear. A very rude gear. Now, there's one delve left that none of us have finished, and I'd like to drink to it before we try.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.0: Beneath the Skyforge, in a hollow of rock, Skjor waits by a stone basin. Behind him stands a great wolf with Aela's eyes.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.1: The Circle carries a gift. Some call it a curse. Drink, and you become one of us in blood as well as name.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.2: The blood burns. For a moment the world smells of rain and fear, and you hear every heartbeat in Whiterun.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.3: You will hunt now, and you will never be cold again.
story.skycraft.scene.vaermina.0: You walk in my dream, little thing. Erandur betrayed me once. Will you betray him, and take my Skull?
story.skycraft.scene.vale.0: Through Darkfall Cave the snow gives way to a hidden valley of waterfalls and pale trees, lit by a sun that never seems to set.
story.skycraft.scene.vale.1: You've come for the bow. Many came. The Snow Elves made sure none returned.
story.skycraft.scene.vg_hall_burning.0: Smoke rises over the Hall of the Vigilant. The doors hang open, and on the snow outside lie Vigilants in their grey robes, very still.
story.skycraft.scene.vg_hall_burning.1: They came at dusk, more than I have ever seen together. A lord of the Volkihar leads them. He is still inside. Stendarr guide your hand.
story.skycraft.scene.vg_hand_of_stendarr: The Hall can be rebuilt. The Vigilants who died here cannot. But they died holding the line, and you finished what they started.
Stendarr's Hand is not a title we give lightly. It goes to the one who stands when everyone else has fallen. Kneel. Rise, Hand of Stendarr.
Outside, the surviving Vigilants have begun clearing the snow from the Hall's steps.
story.skycraft.scene.voyage.0: The Northern Maiden noses out of Windhelm's harbor and turns north and east, into the Sea of Ghosts. Two days later, ash falls on the deck.
story.skycraft.scene.voyage.1: Raven Rock: a Dunmer town under a sky the color of an old bruise. Red Mountain smokes on the horizon.
story.skycraft.scene.whiterun_falls_legi: The rebels are breaking! Hold the gate! Whiterun stands with the Empire!
So be it. Whiterun has chosen. Gods help us all.
story.skycraft.scene.whiterun_falls_stor: The gate's down! For Skyrim! Whiterun is free!
Enough. Whiterun yields. Tell Ulfric he has his city.
story.skycraft.scene.windhelm_falls.0: The Palace of the Kings is quiet. Ulfric Stormcloak kneels in his own throne room and does not ask for mercy.
story.skycraft.scene.windhelm_falls.1: It's over. Skyrim stays in the Empire. Make sure the soldiers know who won this for them.
story.skycraft.scene.wrothgar.0: The mountain does not care who your parents were. Climb it, and kill what lives at the top. Then you are Orsimer enough for me.
